articles.title: Embark Backed Off Arc Raiders Monthly Updates To Stop Burnout
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
	
	
	
Embark Backed Off Arc Raiders Monthly Updates To Stop Burnout
Since its launch in late 2025, Arc Raiders has been a commanding presence in the extraction shooter genre, at one point peaking at over 480,000 concurrent players. Embark has earned its player count partially by listening to its community's needs and by issuing frequent updates to fix issues, introduce fresh gameplay mechanics, and update content—until a recent change to the development cycle that will see less frequent updates. In a recent interview with Game Developer, Arc Raiders executive producer, Aleksander Grøndal, expanded on the studio's justification for the change in update frequency and how the game's dev team now approaches updates.
The team is super tired. We're putting out content as fast as we can, but it's not enough, and perhaps it wasn't necessarily interesting enough as well. I'm proud of what we achieved during the first four months of this year, but at the same time, I think we have to be honest at looking at some of the impacts of that.
Grøndal explains that going from the pre-release development workflow to maintaining a live-service game was even more challenging than he had expected, and that the subsequent upkeep of the game has been so taxing on the Embark development team that content ended up having to be cut from Arc Raiders in order to maintain the update schedule before the change in May that saw the studio shift to a major update twice a year with smaller patches and balance fixes in between.
Transitioning to live service is going to be fucking hard. Everyone said that to me. I've even said that to other people. I was mentally prepared for it to be hard—but I wasn't completely prepared for how hard it was. When you build a game up until launch, you build, and you test, and you build, and you test, and you fix things and measure results. So the way that we've been building video games was based on that idea—but now the demands of the players are really high we feel like we really can't go much faster. 
At the end of the day, Embark ended up with a development team that was unhappy and overworked, and a gaming community that was, by Grøndal's own admission, becoming more and more disgruntled with the quality and substance of updates. Even Grøndal admits that he was burnt out, and in order to both protect Embark's employees and to maintain the quality of the output of the studio, updates were scaled back and scope was decreased
We talk about burnout, and it's obviously bad, but being burned out feels super shitty to be honest. It's terrible. I don't recommend it to anyone. Also, it means we lose good people who might be out for a very long time. 
		
		Source:
				Game Developer			
	
	
	
		
	
		
The team is super tired. We're putting out content as fast as we can, but it's not enough, and perhaps it wasn't necessarily interesting enough as well. I'm proud of what we achieved during the first four months of this year, but at the same time, I think we have to be honest at looking at some of the impacts of that.
Transitioning to live service is going to be fucking hard. Everyone said that to me. I've even said that to other people. I was mentally prepared for it to be hard—but I wasn't completely prepared for how hard it was. When you build a game up until launch, you build, and you test, and you build, and you test, and you fix things and measure results. So the way that we've been building video games was based on that idea—but now the demands of the players are really high we feel like we really can't go much faster. 
We didn't have the time. You also have a lot of the cost of just maintaining the game—implementing bug fixes, exploits, and other constraints. We were constantly overshooting our capacity and so it was hard to plan when there's so much to do. There's a lot of maintenance and cleanup.
We talk about burnout, and it's obviously bad, but being burned out feels super shitty to be honest. It's terrible. I don't recommend it to anyone. Also, it means we lose good people who might be out for a very long time. 
It's very important for us to create a framework that allows us to be creative while having a good work-life balance. If we think long-term about this product—not just in small increments but big-picture stuff—we need all of these great people. Those are the people who built Arc Raiders in the first place.
2 Comments on Embark Backed Off Arc Raiders Monthly Updates To Stop Burnout
What, exactly, did you think was going to happen?
We need to take down the pace a bit at times I think. That doesn't mean being slow and sloppy, but avoiding burnout and have time to contemplate and be thoughtful also about work even if there are people waiting for you, so to speak.

articles.title: I tested the Acemagic K5, a mini PC that's exceptional and diabolical
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The K5 is exceptional in some respects and diabolical in others. Without a doubt, the new Wild Lake silicon is a significant step up from what came before, but it has too few PCIe lanes to be truly useful. But then, if it had those, it might be better than some Core Ultra platforms.
Reasons to buy
- +Core 5 320 performance
- +Easy internal access
- +Dual M.2 2280 slots
- +Plenty of USB ports
Reasons to avoid
- -Mostly plastic construction
- -No USB 4.0 or Thunderbolt
- -PCIe Gen3 x4 drive in a Gen4 slot
Why you can trust TechRadar
Acemagic K5: 30-second review
When this hardware first came to me, it was called the Acemagic KRON mini K5, but somewhere along the line it got rebranded as just the plain old K5.
Built around Intel's Core 5 Processor 320, a chip better known by its original codename, Wildcat Lake. This is the interesting bit. It is Intel's first outing for the 18A process on a mainstream mini PC part, and that matters more than the modest core count suggests.
Six cores split two ways sit at the heart of this silicon. Two performance cores handle the heavy lifting, while four efficient cores take on background tasks and keep power draw sensible. Turbo tops out at 4.6GHz, which is plenty for a machine this size.
The headline figure is AI throughput. ACEMAGIC quotes 40 TOPS across the whole platform, with the NPU alone good for 16 TOPS and the Xe graphics core contributing up to 20 TOPS of its own. That puts local AI tasks such as background blur, transcription and on-device image processing well within reach, without leaning on the cloud.
However, the minimum requirement to run even Copilot locally is 47 TOPS, so it's best suited to simple models.
Memory has moved on too. LPDDR5 running at 6400MT/s replaces the LPDDR4X seen on older ACEMAGIC boxes, and that faster memory feeds both the CPU and the integrated Xe graphics more efficiently. The trade-off is that the memory is soldered down, so what it comes with, 16GB in this instance, is all it will ever have.
The downside is that this NUC costs closer to mid-spec hardware, but it lacks USB4 ports, and its NVMe slots are only Gen4 x2. Cheaper Intel and AMD platforms offer USB4 and NVMe Gen4 x4 slots, but they use older technology.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Once more Wildcat Lake systems enter the market, hopefully prices will come down, but it seems overpriced for the specs it offers.
It's never going to be the best mini PC, but it is an improvement over what technology it replaces.
Acemagic K5: Price and availability
- How much does it cost? From $559
- When is it out? Shipping from mid-October 2026
- Where can you get it? You can get it directly from Acemagic
At the time of writing, the K5 is available for pre-order directly from Acemagic.com, but it seems likely that after its mid-October launch, it will also be purchasable from online retailers.
The US asking price is $559 for the only SKU, which has the Intel Core 5 320 CPU, 16GB of LPDDR5 memory and a 512GB SSD.
In the EU, two SKUs are coming on the 12th of October: one matching the US spec and another with the Intel Core 3 304 CPU, 12GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage. These are €549 and €349, respectively.
Right now, the K5 isn’t listed on the UK pages, but that’s likely to change in the coming weeks.
As I’ve already mentioned, the Wild Lake silicon is new, and other system makers are still readying their Wild Lake systems.
However, I found that Beelink has the EQ mini, which uses the Wildcat Lake Core 3 304 and comes with 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage for $429. The 304 CPU has only five cores, less GPU and AI power, and a lower clock speed than the 320.
The only other brand shipping a machine based on the Core 5 320 is ASRock, with its Industrial NUC BOX-320. But that’s a quote-only solution that can come with 64GB of RAM and dual 2.5GbE LAN ports, so it’s unlikely to be cheap.
Overall, it's hard to tell whether the K5 will align with what system makers will ask for on this platform, but I’d hope it's less than this. The machines it replaces used the Core 3 N305, and those were, until memory became stupidly expensive, mostly below $300.
- Value: 3 / 5
Acemagic K5: Specs
| Acemagic K5 Specifications |  | 
|---|---|
| CPU | Intel Core 5 Processor 320 (Wildcat Lake), 2 performance cores plus 4 efficient cores, 6 threads, Intel 18A process | 
| Clock speed | 1.4GHz base, up to 4.6GHz turbo | 
| Cache | 6MB Intel Smart Cache | 
| NPU | Up to 16 TOPS (Int8) | 
| Platform AI total | Up to 40 TOPS across CPU, GPU and NPU | 
| GPU | Intel Xe graphics, 2 Xe cores, up to 2.5GHz, up to 20 TOPS AI compute | 
| Memory | 16GB LPDDR5 6400MT/s, onboard and non-upgradable | 
| Primary storage | 512GB M.2 2280 NVMe SSD (PCIe Gen3 x4) | 
| Expansion storage | 1x M.2 2280 NVMe, each on a PCIe 4.0 x2 link | 
| Wireless | WiFi 6 | 
| Bluetooth | Bluetooth 5.2 (M.2 2230 module) | 
| Wired networking | 1x 2.5GbE LAN, auto-negotiating down to 10Mbps | 
| HDMI | 1x HDMI 2.0, up to 4K at 60Hz | 
| DisplayPort | 1x DP 1.4, up to 4K at 60Hz | 
| USB-C video | DP 1.4 Alt Mode, up to 4K at 60Hz, alongside USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 data at up to 20Gbps and USB PD 100W input | 
| Audio | 1x 3.5mm jack | 
| USB-A front | 2x USB 3.2 Gen 2, 10Gbps | 
| USB-A rear | 4x USB 3.2 Gen 1, 5Gbps | 
| USB-C | 1x, shared video, data and 100W power input duties as above | 
| Other | 1x DC power input, 1x power button | 
| Dimensions | 128 x 128 x 41.3mm | 
| Power input | DC 19V, 3.42A, up to 25W TDP design | 
| Cooling | 80mm x 10mm fan, aluminium heatsink, dual air outlets, rated at 2000rpm and above | 
| Operating system | Windows 11 Pro | 
| Warranty | Two years | 
Acemagic K5: Design
- Plastic enclosure
- Easy access
- No USB 4
Acemagic has made systems with metal enclosures, but the K5 isn’t one of them. This is mostly plastic, and no amount of metallic paint is going to make people think otherwise.
The advantage of that material is that the K5 is remarkably light, and with a provided VESA bracket, it's remarkably easy to mount this hardware to the back of a monitor.
The chassis itself is tiny, at 128 by 128 by 41.3mm, yet ACEMAGIC has kept the TDP down to 25W. That should mean quiet running and low running costs, useful for anyone who wants a machine parked on a desk all day rather than tucked away and forgotten.
Access to the internals looks easy, since Acemagic has a small switch on the rear that slides to unlock the top of the case. But those expecting tool-less entry are soon disappointed: under the lid is a panel that needs four screws removed before you can reach the top of the motherboard.
That plate helps distribute heat from the SSDs and has a thermal pad, so you still need to pry it off even after removing the screws.
Once you get past those hurdles, you can reach the M.2 slots, and there are three. Two are the conventional 2280 variety; one is occupied by Windows 11 Pro, and the third is 2242 and occupied by the WiFi module.
Two 2280 M.2 slots sound great on paper, but there is a caveat we’ll get to later.
There is no memory access because the LPDDR5 used in this machine is soldered to the mainboard.
Moving back to the outside, ports are limited to the front and back, with the sides reserved for ventilation slots.
The front has a power button that self-illuminates with “POWER” when you press it to start the system, a small touch I liked. Also front-facing are two USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports, a USB-C 3.2 Gen 2x2 port and a 3.5mm audio jack.
On the rear are four more USB-A ports, all USB 3.2 Gen 1 (5Gbps), one each of HDMI 2.0 and DisplayPort and a single 2.5GbE LAN port. It also has a security slot on the rear, which, given how pocketable this machine is, might be worth using.
That single USB-C does a lot of work here. It carries video through DP Alt Mode, shifts data at up to 20Gbps over USB 3.2 Gen 2x2, and accepts up to 100W of power delivery. But that last specification makes zero sense, as you can’t power this PC with USB-C.
Placing it on the front, I assume you are meant to use it to charge phones and laptops, but that would be 100W output, not input. But this port doesn’t charge, which is confusing.
A bigger issue is that there is no USB4, and that is becoming something people expect, even if it’s only one port.
This problem, and a few others, come down to one part of the Wildcat Lake architecture that Intel didn’t improve enough.
- Design: 4 / 5
Acemagic K5: Features
- Wild Lake Core 5 320
- LPDDR5 Memory
- Short on PCIe lanes
The heart of this PC is a new processor series from Intel, which had the codename Wildcat Lake. This is a logical evolution of the products that were once in the Atom product lineup, and then went through a major revamp to become the N100, N150 and N305.
These were initially either two or four-core processors made for light-duty and embedded applications. Because they were cheap, they also ended up in some NUC enclosures, for those who didn’t need a powerful platform.
Somewhere along this path, Intel released the N300 with 8 cores, and the scope of what these systems could do expanded significantly.
But Intel has now abandoned that direction, the one where the chips all used E-cores (E for efficiency), operated with 7W or 15W of power and used the old UHD graphics.
The Core 5 320 has six cores. Two of these are now P-cores, designed for performance, alongside four E-cores.
Its power envelope starts at 15W and can be up to 54W, and where the N300 topped out at 3.8GHz, this new 18A silicon can run at 4.6GHz in boost mode.
With these attributes, it has significantly higher single-core and multi-core performance (roughly doubling the aggregate capability of entry-level N-series chips) thanks to its higher clock speeds and dedicated performance cores.
Which begs the obvious question: if it's that much better, where does that put the lower-specification Core Ultra chips? Well, Intel made sure it wouldn’t bother them, in a somewhat insidious way.
The PCIe lane budget is the catch, and it undermines many of the positive aspects of this series. On paper, the Core 5 320 has PCIe 4.0 instead of the PCIe 3.0 its predecessors got, so each lane has twice the bandwidth. But Intel gave it only six lanes, compared to the nine lanes in the Alder Lake-N series it replaces. Yes, another 33% more bandwidth, but the N300 was PCIe lane-starved to begin with.
To put that into perspective, a typical AMD Ryzen 5 mobile CPU has 20 lanes out of 24, and even on older models with PCIe 3.0, that’s more actual lanes and bandwidth than the Core 5 320. To be accurate, it’s 66% more.
This shortfall is not an Acemagic oversight but a Wildcat Lake platform limitation. Compact, low-power chips like this one get a smaller pool of PCIe lanes to share across storage, networking, and USB, and something has to give. Here, storage draws the short straw.
For everyday use, browsing, office work and light content creation, this will go largely unnoticed. For anyone hoping to drop in a fast PCIe 4.0 x4 drive and get full speed for large file transfers or video editing scratc
- Features: 3 / 5
Acemagic K5: Performance
| Mini PC | Row 0 - Cell 1 | Acemagic K5 | Beelink ME mini | 
| CPU | Row 1 - Cell 1 | Intel Core 5 320 | Intel N150 | 
| Cores/Threads |  | 6C 6T | 4C 4T | 
| RAM | Row 3 - Cell 1 | 16GB LPDDR5 6400 | 12GB LPDRR5 (1x 12GB) | 
| SSD | Row 4 - Cell 1 | 512GB G932E5 | 64GB eMMC + 2TB Crucial P3 Plus SSD | 
| Graphics | Row 5 - Cell 1 | Intel Xe3 Graphics (Wildcat Lake) | Intel Graphics 730 (EU24) | 
| 3DMark | WildLife | 11018 | 2298 | 
| Row 7 - Cell 0 | FireStrike | 3508 | 732 | 
| Row 8 - Cell 0 | TimeSpy | 1693 | 293 | 
| Row 9 - Cell 0 | S.Nomad | 1254 | 188 | 
| Cine24 | Single | 110 | 56 | 
| Row 11 - Cell 0 | Multi | 402 | 135 | 
| Row 12 - Cell 0 | Ratio | 3.64 | 2.4 | 
| GeekBench 6 | Single | 2559 | 1103 | 
| Row 14 - Cell 0 | Multi | 7852 | 2334 | 
| Row 15 - Cell 0 | OpenCL | 12764 | 3908 | 
| Row 16 - Cell 0 | Vulkan | 14273 | 4354 | 
| CrystalDisk | Read MB/s | 1786 | 1731 | 
| Row 18 - Cell 0 | Write MB/s | 1748 | 1686 | 
| PCMark 10 | Office | 6280 | 2781 | 
| WEI | Score | 8.1 | 5.6 | 
It was hard to decide which machine spec to compare the K5 with, since it’s an entirely new platform.
But since this is designed to replace the old N100 and N300 tier in the Intel stable, I found an N150-powered mini PC, the Beelink ME mini, that seemed appropriate.
Except in most respects, the Wildcat Lake machine eats the Twin Lake (Alder Lake-N refresh) architecture for breakfast.
In fact, if we take the single-core benchmarks in isolation, the Core 5 320 is faster than the Intel Core Ultra 5 125H, and for graphics it's faster than the Intel Core i7 12650H.
The dramatic difference we see against Twin Lake is because that platform used only Gracemont efficiency cores, had fewer cores, offered only single-channel memory support, used an Intel UHD graphics GPU, and had no NPU support.
This new Wildcat Lake generation has two performance cores and four efficiency cores, dual-channel DDR5 memory, Intel Xe3 graphics (two Xe cores), and an integrated NPU.
But those advantages come at a power cost: while the Beelink ME mini operated within a 9-15W budget, the Acemagic K5 runs 9-25W, and some systems running this chip will likely turbo to 35W.
But it’s easy to get carried away by all the performance benefits this generation brings and miss a rather obvious hole Intel left unpatched in the good ship Wildcat Lake.
Both machines share one horrible aspect: abysmal SSD performance. And it's for precisely the same reason.
While Intel was handing out all the new technology in the memory management, cores, GPU and NPU departments, they failed to properly address one critical area, PCIe lanes.
The Twin Lake architecture supported 9 PCIe 3.0 lanes, and the new Wildcat Lake supports 6 PCIe 4.0 lanes. Because PCIe 4.0 has double the bandwidth of PCIe 3.0, that’s the modern equivalent of 12 PCIe 3.0 lanes.
But with a 2.5GbE LAN port and seven USB ports, that eats up bandwidth to the point where there aren’t enough PCIe lanes to properly support the M.2 NVMe slots.
These slots are both PCIe 4.0 x2, and that’s a problem.
As the benchmarks reveal, the speed of the system drive is less than 1800MB/s in both read and write. But the drive's specification is double that speed.
The drive is a Gen3 drive, but the M.2 slot is Gen4, and the result is that it gets two lanes of PCIe, and two lanes of Gen3 is about 1800MB/s. That mistake is on Acemagic, because a Gen4 drive would be twice as fast. Not Gen4 x4 fast, since it only has two lanes, but twice as fast as the Gen3 drive Acemagic installed.
This is all somewhat frustrating. Intel built a punchy six-core system with excellent single-core performance and reasonable GPU output, and then kneecapped it effectively with limited PCIe lanes. And Acemagic put the wrong type of NVMe drive in one, regrettably.
- Performance: 3.5 / 5
Acemagic K5: Final verdict
As you may have gathered, the K5 is a mixed bag. But aside from one issue I can put down to Acemagic, most of the problems are Intel’s.
The more I looked at this system, the more I came to the conclusion that Intel realised these low-end chips were going to be too good, so they made sure they couldn’t be used more broadly by limiting the number of PCIe lanes.
Evidently, USB4 or Gen x4 M.2 slots on the Core 5 320 would have threatened Core Ultra models, so they made sure it was unlikely to have them.
Acemagic, for their part, did the best they could with this platform, with the exception of the Gen3 NVMe drive, which was a cost saving too far.
If this system were ever to be around $400, I’d recommend it for general office use, but its launch price makes it compete with the likes of the GMKtec M6 Ultra Mini PC. That’s a $459.99 system powered by an AMD Ryzen 5 7640HS (6 cores, 12 threads) with dual Gen4 x4 M.2 slots, USB4, dual 2.5GbE LAN ports and slotted SODIMM DDR5 memory that can be upgraded to 128GB.
When you compare the two options, the Acemagic K5 looks like it's been priced above what its specifications can justify.
Should you buy a Acemagic K5?
| Value | Seems expensive for the specifications | 3 / 5 | 
| Design | Mostly plastic construction with easy-ish internal access | 4 / 5 | 
| Features | Great new Wildcat Lake CPU undermined by lack of PCIe lanes | 3 / 5 | 
| Performance | An excellent single-core performer, but the Gen3 NVMe drive is slowed down in a Gen4 slot | 3.5 / 5 | 
| Overall | What could be a useful general-purpose system, if it can get much cheaper than the launch price. | 3.5 / 5 | 
Buy it if...
You must have the latest tech
The Wildcat Lake CPU in this system is impressive and shows that Intel can deliver performance and efficiency if they want. It’s a dramatic improvement over the old N-series silicon.
You need lots of USB
With two USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports on this design and another four Gen1, this machine has plenty of ports for external devices without the need to attach a dock.
Don't buy it if...
You need USB4 or Thunderbolt
While the K5 has plenty of USB, it doesn’t support Thunderbolt or USB 4.0. For those using those technologies, that could be a deal-breaker.
You need high-performance NVMe
This machine comes with a Gen3 NVMe that lives in a Gen4 slot, halving its performance. But even with a Gen4 drive, the dual-lane configuration only allows for a maximum of about 3800MB/s transfer. It doesn’t matter what drive you put inside this machine; it won’t go any faster.
Also Consider
GMKtec K6 Ultra
A mid-level AMD system that sports an AMD Ryzen 5 7640HS processor, up to 32GB of RAM and dual Gen4 x4 M.2 slots. This hardware shows what’s possible when you have 20 PCIe lanes. Also available in a barebones configuration if you have RAM and SSDs spare.
Check out our GMKtec K6 Ultra review
Acemagic K1
Those wanting a decent PC that can run any office tasks and surf the internet should consider the previous Acemagic design, the K1. It comes in two variants: one that uses the Intel Core i5-12600H, and another much more affordable model that’s built around the AMD Ryzen 5 or Ryzen 7 platforms.
The top-spec model uses the Ryzen 7 773OU CPU, comes with 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD, and costs a little over $400. A good price for a machine with an 8-core, 16-thread CPU.
Check out our AceMagic K1 (Intel version) review
For more professional hardware, we've reviewed the best business computers.
Mark is an expert on 3D printers, drones and phones. He also covers storage, including SSDs, NAS drives and portable hard drives. He started writing in 1986 and has contributed to MicroMart, PC Format, 3D World, among others.

articles.title: TVs superam PCs e viram novo carrinho de compras • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
TVs superam PCs e viram novo carrinho de compras
TV cresce frente aos desktops enquanto o celular se isola como meio preferido para compras online.
As funções de interatividade nas smart TVs que permitem compras diretamente no aparelho parecem estar fazendo algum efeito. Pela primeira vez, as compras digitais realizadas por meio de TVs superaram computadores de mesa e tablets, refletindo o avanço desses recursos em transmissões e apps de streaming.
A participação dos desktops caiu de 13% em 2024 para 11% no ano passado e 10% em 2026, segundo a 10ª edição do relatório The Future Shopper, da agência de publicidade VML, que ouviu 28 mil consumidores de 17 países, incluindo o Brasil.
O uso das TVs saltou de 8% nos dois últimos anos para 11% em 2026, enquanto o tablet, que mantinha resultados iguais aos da televisão em 2024 e 2025, caiu para 7%. Essa realidade pode crescer por aqui com a expansão da TV 3.0, tecnologia que começou a ser implementada neste ano e tem a interatividade na programação ao vivo – incluindo compras – como um dos seus pilares.
Ao mesmo tempo, a presença de computadores nos lares brasileiros tem sido mínima. Apenas 14% das casas com algum tipo de computador possuem desktops, segundo levantamento divulgado pela Anatel no ano passado. Com o aumento dos preços de componentes de PCs, pela crise no setor de semicondutores, pode não ter havido uma grande mudança nesse sentido.
A mudança joga as TVs para a terceira posição entre os dispositivos mais usados para compras online, mas o número ainda é muito abaixo das compras via celular, com 40% de participação. O ranking ficou assim:
Mesmo com a liderança dos smartphones, a pesquisa aponta problemas na experiência de compra. Cerca de 40% dos entrevistados afirmaram que comprar pelo celular ainda é pior do que pelo computador, enquanto 34% reclamaram especificamente do processo de finalização da compra.
Mais da metade dos consumidores (55%) também disse que marcas e varejistas deveriam trabalhar mais para melhorar a navegação em dispositivos móveis. Outro dado mostra o impacto do excesso de estímulos: 50% dos entrevistas já desinstalaram aplicativos de compras por causa da quantidade de notificações.
A pesquisa também traz o cenário da preferência por compras online ou presenciais. A média global de consumo no comércio eletrônico caiu para 51% neste ano, após estagnar em 53% no último biênio. O número é também o menor desde 2021, quando, durante a pandemia, chegou a 61%.
Mas o Brasil segue engajado nas plataformas online, onde 58% dos gastos dos consumidores são feitos, contra 42% no varejo físico. É o segundo país que mais consome na inernet, atrás apenas da China (59%), enquanto outras nações sul-americanas, como Colômbia e Argentina, chegam a 44% e 47%, respectivamente.
As IAs também têm aparecido como intermediadoras entre o consumidor e a compra, e elas têm ganhado espaço. A parcelo dos entrevistados que já usou alguma dessas ferramentas chegou a 82% em 2026, com o ChatGPT liderando a preferência dos entrevistados frente ao Gemini: 48% contra 37%.
Além de tirar dúvidas, as plataformas ajudam os consumidores a entender o que procuram e comparar preços. 45% disseram estar entusiasmados com IAs agênticas que procurem o melhor preço em seu nome, algo que as principais desenvolvedores tentam implementar nos modelos mais recentes. Quem prefere a pesquisa manual pode ficar atento aos Achados do Tecnoblog.

articles.title: Creadores de GTA 5 impiden el proyecto que buscaba llevar el juego a teléfonos Android
articles.text:
Take-Two Interactive, casa matriz de Rockstar Games, logró la cancelación definitiva del proyecto que buscaba llevar Grand Theft Auto 5 (GTA 5) a dispositivos Android de forma no oficial. El estudio independiente detrás del desarrollo, Paralympics Productions, anunció el cierre de sus operaciones tras recibir una carta de cese y desistimiento por parte de la compañía.
El líder del proyecto, que opera bajo el nombre de usuario Mojso, comunicó la noticia a través de la red social X (antes Twitter). Según su publicación, el estudio dejará de operar el próximo sábado 3 de octubre, en cumplimiento con el requerimiento extrajudicial exigido por Take-Two.
PUBLICIDAD
“Paralympics Productions dejará de operar el 3 de octubre. Gracias a todos los que nos apoyaron en tiempos difíciles y durante un desarrollo tan prolongado. Lamento no haber cumplido con sus expectativas y dejarlos con las manos vacías. Agradezco la clemencia de Take-Two, por lo que este es el fin definitivo”, escribió Mojso en su mensaje de despedida.
Un desarrollo que buscaba ejecutar el juego de forma nativa
Los reportes sobre este proyecto independiente comenzaron a circular a mediados de septiembre. La iniciativa provenía del mismo equipo que había desarrollado anteriormente una versión experimental de GTA 5 para Nintendo Switch, otra consola en la que el título original nunca fue lanzado de manera oficial.
PUBLICIDAD
A diferencia de una simple emulación, la propuesta de Paralympics Productions consistía en ejecutar el videojuego de forma nativa en dispositivos Android, sin extenderse a la plataforma iOS. El equipo incluso había publicado un listado de especificaciones mínimas de hardware necesarias para su instalación, aunque desde el inicio existían dudas sobre la viabilidad del proyecto frente a una eventual respuesta legal de la desarrolladora original.
Según se informó en su momento, el port no oficial habría utilizado partes del código fuente de GTA 5 filtrado en 2023. Desde el estudio no confirmaron este punto de manera directa, aunque reconocieron que Take-Two contaba con “argumentos sólidos” para su reclamo, motivo por el cual decidieron no disputarlo.
PUBLICIDAD
El desafío público que precedió al cierre
El conflicto se intensificó después de un mensaje publicado por Mojso el 21 de septiembre, en el que citó una captura de los términos de uso actualizados de la franquicia Grand Theft Auto con un comentario desafiante: “Ponme a prueba, Rockstar”.
El fragmento citado por el propio desarrollador correspondía a una cláusula específica de los términos oficiales de Rockstar Games y su editora, Take-Two Interactive, que establece: “No modifiques nuestros juegos para que funcionen en consolas, dispositivos de hardware u otras plataformas en las que no hayan sido lanzados oficialmente por Rockstar Games”.
Apenas una semana después de esa publicación, Mojso confirmó el cierre definitivo de Paralympics Productions. La compañía ya había advertido de forma pública sobre las consecuencias de modificar sus juegos sin autorización, una postura que aplicó anteriormente contra otros proyectos de modding, entre ellos las remasterizaciones no oficiales de GTA Vice City y GTA San Andreas realizadas por aficionados.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin código fuente disponible tras el cierre
Rockstar Games y Take-Two Interactive mantienen una política estricta en la protección de sus propiedades intelectuales, lo que habría hecho prácticamente imposible distribuir una versión no oficial de GTA 5 en Android de manera segura y sostenida en el tiempo.
Con la cancelación confirmada, los desarrolladores de Paralympics Productions también descartaron la posibilidad de distribuir el código fuente del proyecto, con el objetivo de evitar complicaciones legales adicionales. El cierre del estudio quedará formalizado el próximo sábado 3 de octubre, fecha límite establecida por la propia empresa demandante para cumplir con el cese de operaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Agent gateway lets Okta police AI agent runtime actions - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Okta moves inline to police what AI agents actually do
An agent gateway moves identity security beyond deciding who gets through the front door to governing what autonomous AI agents do once inside. By sitting in the path of attempted actions, the gateway can enforce authorization decisions at runtime.
Okta Inc. recently launched an AI agent runtime gateway as part of its broader approach to securing autonomous systems. The architecture marks a new role for the identity provider, according to Ric Smith (pictured), president of products and technology at Okta.
“That is a very different transition for Okta,” he said. “Dominantly, we had not been inline, so with us moving in that direction, it means that we can do a lot more decision-making in terms of what we authorize.”
Smith spoke with theCUBE Research’s Krista Case and co-host Rebecca Knight at Okta’s Oktane event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed runtime threat detection, intent-based authorization and how Okta is expanding further into cybersecurity. (* Disclosure below.)
Why an agent gateway puts Okta in the runtime path
Being inline also lets Okta watch for threats rather than simply grant permissions. That logic drove the company’s acquisition of Permiso Security, which adds detection capabilities as Okta expands further into cybersecurity, according to Smith. Full visibility into an agent’s behavior, however, requires observing both the prompt entering the model and the actions it proposes.
“You really have to sit in two positions around these models,” he said. “One is on the front end of it so that you can capture the conversation being presented. Then, based on the Gateway that we’ve already announced, we already sit on the back end of the model where we can capture all of the actions that the model ultimately wants to take and then also make decisions around that.”
Combining those vantage points could allow Okta to judge whether a proposed action should proceed, Smith explained. In 2027, the company plans to add intent-based authorization to its agent gateway, using an agent’s context and permitted tools to inform access decisions. Determining how narrowly to scope those permissions without blocking legitimate work remains an open research question.
“It’s a hard problem for us to solve, and so that’s why we’re hard at work doing all the research around it,” Smith said. “But we think that is pay dirt in terms of what actually has to happen with the agent workforce.”

articles.title: Toujours plus massif, mais ultra performant : on a testé l'iPhone 18 Pro d'Apple
articles.text:

L'iPhone 18 Pro n'arrive pas seul sur le marché. Comme à son habitude, Apple l'accompagne d'un iPhone 18 Pro Max, un smartphone sans concession, mais au format XXL.
La cuvée d’iPhone monobloc pour la rentrée 2026 ne compte que deux appareils : l’iPhone 18 Pro et sa déclinaison Pro Max, l’iPhone 18 classique ayant été évincé de la keynote de septembre pour mieux offrir à l’iPhone Duo pliant les feux des projecteurs. L’iPhone 18 Pro, testé par Les Numériques, cumule les atouts si l’on excepte son tarif de lancement, bien entendu. L’iPhone 18 Pro Max reprend la même recette puisqu’Apple ne distingue plus ses appareils Pro et Pro Max depuis sa génération 16.
Entre les deux modèles, l’essentiel de la différence tient donc à un format agrandi qui autorise l’intégration d’une batterie plus généreuse, tandis que la puce A20, le boîtier en aluminium (paré de nouvelles couleurs), le triple module photo dorsal (dont un grand-angle à ouverture variable) et les fonctionnalités propres à iOS 27 sont semblables.
Côté “douloureuse”, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max se classe parmi les smartphones les plus onéreux du marché. Apple le facture 1629 € en version 256 Go, 1879 € en 512 Go, 2379 € en 1 To et enfin 3129 € en 2 To. Un appareil luxueux qui ne peut donc s’autoriser aucun compromis. Nous l'avons bien entendu testé sous iOS 27.
Entre l’iPhone 18 Pro et le 18 Pro Max qui nous intéresse ici, la distinction se fait au niveau du format. Le Pro Max opte pour un gabarit imposant (163,4 x 78 x 8,8 mm), identique à celui du 17 Pro Max en 2025. En revanche, il gagne quelques grammes sur la balance : il pèse 249 g, soit 16 g de plus que l’iPhone 17 Pro Max et 22 g de plus que l’iPhone 16 Pro Max. C’est davantage que les mastodontes du marché (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra et ses 214 g, Oppo Find X9 Ultra à 235 g), et cela commence à faire beaucoup. Dans une poche, si la vôtre vous permet de l’accueillir, il ne passe pas inaperçu et impose une utilisation à deux mains pour éviter les chutes malencontreuses.
Pour le reste, Apple propose une expérience semblable à celle du 18 Pro. Le boîtier en aluminium, qui accueille un “plateau” photo dorsal, est similaire et adopte les mêmes coloris (bordeaux, bleu glacier, noir et gris). Les tranches arrondies sont confortables en main et l’on a droit à la fois au bouton photo situé sur la tranche droite et à la touche action sur le flanc gauche. La certification IP68 signale la résistance du boîtier à l’immersion, et on retrouve une vitre Ceramic Shield 2 pour en protéger l’écran des rayures.
La version européenne de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max est pourvue d’un port nano-SIM, à la différence de son homologue étasunienne qui mise uniquement sur l’eSIM. En revanche, tous ont droit au wifi 7, au Bluetooth 6.0, à la charge sans-fil MagSafe à 25 W et à un port USB-C.
Pour aller plus loin :
Apple munit son iPhone 18 Pro Max d’un écran Oled de 6,9 pouces, un afficheur pensé pour le multimédia compte tenu de sa généreuse diagonale. Il affiche une définition de 1320 x 2868 pixels, soit une résolution de 460 ppp, identique à celle de l’iPhone 18 Pro.
Les qualités observées sur le modèle Pro se retrouvent sur le modèle Pro Max qui affiche non seulement une très haute luminosité (encore plus haute d’ailleurs, à 2840 cd/m²), mais reflète peu la lumière (réflectance de 36 %). Concrètement, cela signifie donc que le smartphone est armé pour assurer une excellente lisibilité, même lorsqu’il est utilisé en plein soleil.
La calibration du smartphone est convaincante, bien que l’appareil ne soit pas 100 % parfait. On relève un delta E faible, limité à 1,69 (c’est un peu plus que les 1,07 de l’iPhone 18 Pro, mais bien en deçà du seuil de 3 à partir duquel les dérives de couleurs sont perceptibles par l’œil humain). En contrepartie, la température des couleurs est un peu élevée, à 6970 K, quand l’objectif est de tendre vers 6500 K, sachant que la maîtrise est souvent moindre lorsque les dalles s’agrandissent. Néanmoins, hormis cette colorimétrie un peu fraîche, il y a vraiment peu à redire sur l'afficheur de l'iPhone 18 Pro Max.
Gravée en 2 nm, la puce A20 Pro inaugure une nouvelle ère dans l’écosystème d’Apple. Munie de six cœurs CPU et de sept cœurs graphiques, la puce mobile se paie le luxe d’atteindre des performances dignes des puces M intégrées aux Mac de la Pomme. Nous avons d’ailleurs dédié à cette thématique un comparatif des performances réalisées par l’A20 Pro et par diverses puces Apple Silicon M.
Ajoutons que le chipset, particulièrement puissant, est flanqué d’une chambre à vapeur efficace, même si le smartphone chauffe lorsque l’A20 est sollicité. On le lui pardonne compte tenu de la puissance de l'appareil.
Fiche technique en main, la configuration photo de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max ne montre aucun bouleversement majeur par rapport à la génération précédente. On retrouve le triptyque de capteurs de 48 mégapixels (Mpx) : un grand-angle, un ultra grand-angle et un téléobjectif 4x (équivalent 100 mm) — le grossissement 8x vanté par la marque reste un simple recadrage numérique du module 4x.
La vraie rupture, outre le traitement d'image retravaillé, réside dans l'intégration d’un diaphragme à ouverture variable sur l'objectif principal. Kaput l'ouverture fixe à f/1,8 de l'iPhone 17 Pro Max : la lentille oscille désormais entre f/1,48 et f/4. Au sein de l'app Caméra (remaniée avec l'arrivée d'iOS 27), l'utilisateur a le choix entre quatre valeurs préréglées (f/1,48, f/1,8, f/2,8 et f/4) ou la prise en main automatique par le système.
Cette ouverture vers davantage de réglages manuels mérite d'être saluée chez Apple, historiquement adepte du tout-automatique. Les photographes exigeants pourront exploiter des apps tierces grâce au déverrouillage des API dédiées pour ajuster plus finement ce paramètre. En pratique au quotidien, le système privilégie quasi systématiquement f/1,48 ou f/1,8 de jour comme de nuit. L’intérêt majeur réside surtout dans la possibilité d’obtenir un flou d'arrière-plan optique et naturel sur les portraits sans passer par la simulation algorithmique.
En laissant l’appareil gérer lui-même la prise de vue lors de nos tests en labo, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max s'est calé sur f/1,8 sous un éclairage optimal. Le résultat est irréprochable : les détails sont particulièrement riches, la netteté s'étend jusqu'aux bords de l'image et le piqué gagne en précision sur les finitions (notamment sur nos pastilles de test) par rapport à l'iPhone 17 Pro Max. On note au passage une gestion des contrastes plus adoucie garantissant un rendu global plus naturel. Même si l'évolution par rapport au millésime 2025 reste mesurée, la prestation demeure excellente.
En environnement sombre, l'objectif s’ouvre au maximum à f/1,48 afin de capter un volume de lumière maximal. Malgré une balance des blancs tendant vers des tons plus chauds que sur le 17 Pro Max, le gain en piqué est indéniable. La scène offre un niveau de détail supérieur (notamment sur la cartographie) et la gestion du bruit numérique s’avère nettement plus maîtrisée.
Sur la très courte focale, les avancées se révèlent plus modestes. En plein jour, le module continue d'offrir des clichés de très bonne facture. On remarque certes une légère baisse de piqué en périphérie, ainsi qu'un peu de grain sur les aplats de couleur, mais la prestation globale reste d'un très bon niveau.
C'est à la nuit tombée que l'écart se creuse face au modèle précédent. L'iPhone 18 Pro Max délivre un cliché aux teintes plus chaudes, mais débarrassé du bruit parasite qui entachait les prises de vue du 17 Pro Max. La lisibilité y gagne énormément : les éléments textuels, à l'instar des micro-impressions sur le billet de banque, ressortent bien plus nettement. Seul bémol : un vignettage assez prononcé assombrit la périphérie de l'image.
Le téléobjectif hérite de la même orientation colorimétrique que le capteur principal. L’atténuation des contrastes apporte une touche de naturel bienvenue, tout en conservant une très bonne restitution des détails. On observe un lissage des textures un peu plus marqué qu'au grand-angle sans que cela n'altère l'esthétique générale des clichés.
En basse luminosité, en revanche, les limites du capteur apparaissent vite. Le bruit numérique devient envahissant, dégradant la netteté et affadissant la palette chromatique. Il vaut donc mieux réserver le zoom aux scènes correctement éclairées.
Pour les selfies, Apple reconduit le capteur Center Stage de 18 Mpx (f/1,9) armé du recadrage dynamique automatique. Les clichés ne sont donc pas restitués dans leur définition brute, mais ils profitent d'une exposition maîtrisée, d’une belle précision et des nouveaux Styles photographiques personnalisables.
Sur le terrain de la vidéo, le haut de gamme d'Apple conserve sa position dominante. Capable de filmer jusqu'en 4K à 100 images par seconde (i/s) en Dolby Vision, il met à disposition des créateurs le mode Cinématique, le format Log et une stabilisation redoutable. On apprécie tout particulièrement la fonction de verrouillage du sujet par simple double-tap, idéale pour maintenir une mise au point précise sur une cible en mouvement.
S’il est aussi lourd, c’est également parce qu’il héberge la batterie à la plus haute capacité jamais proposée par Apple. L’iPhone 18 Pro Max intègre un accumulateur estimé à 5391 mAh (capacité nominale) alors que le 17 Pro Max n’excédait pas les 4828 mAh. Le résultat est là : nous avons relevé 33 h 12 min d’utilisation avant extinction, soit un peu plus de 3 h de plus que le 17 Pro Max. De quoi très largement tenir une journée loin de tout chargeur.
En filaire (la charge sans-fil MagSafe est limitée à 25 W), le smartphone demande 1 h 2 min pour une charge complète.
Notre score de durabilité permet de déterminer l'aspect durable du smartphone, autant pour le consommateur que pour l'environnement. Il s'appuie sur des éléments puisés dans l’étiquette énergie mise en place par l’Union européenne (classe énergétique, scores de résistance aux chutes et de réparabilité, nombre de cycles de batterie avant de tomber sous une capacité de 80 % et résistance de l’écran aux rayures). Nous y ajoutons des critères de durabilité (indice de protection IP, connecteurs standards, durée de garantie et des mises à jour…). Vous trouverez tous les détails de l'analyse dans notre article présentant notre score de durabilité.
L'iPhone 18 Pro Max, comme l'iPhone 18 Pro, est une réussite. Sa puce A20 Pro atteint une puissance inégalée à ce jour, son écran ultralumineux délivre une expérience XXL, son volet photo est réussi et il est particulièrement endurant. Si l'on excepte son poids franchement élevé, il n'y a pas grand-chose à lui reprocher.
Le principal concurrent de l'iPhone 18 Pro Max d’Apple est tout bonnement son prédécesseur, qui n'a rien perdu de sa pertinence même un an après sa sortie, et que l'on trouve à tarif moindre. La cohorte des smartphones premium sous Android (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Xiaomi 17 Ultra, Oppo Find X9 Ultra…) constituera une alternative bien plus abordable.

articles.title: Google retire l’option pour revenir à Assistant après le passage à Gemini
articles.text:
Sur Android, Gemini prend la place de Google Assistant et l’option permettant de revenir en arrière disparaît. Le basculement, engagé début septembre, touche aussi les appareils liés au téléphone.
L’appui prolongé sur le bouton d’alimentation ou le balayage depuis un coin de l’écran lance désormais Gemini sur les appareils concernés. 9to5Google qui a vérifié aux États-Unis et en Europe, n’a plus trouvé Google Assistant sur les téléphones et comptes testés. Signal d'un déploiement étendu, pas nécessairement achevé partout.
L’option de retour disparaît des réglages de Gemini
Jusqu’ici, les utilisateurs qui avaient adopté Gemini pouvaient retrouver Google Assistant depuis le menu de leur compte. Le raccourci « Passer à Google Assistant » n’y figure plus avec les versions 17.60 stable et 17.62 bêta de l’application Google. La migration cesse donc d’être un simple choix d’assistant dans les réglages.
Ce retrait arrive après un calendrier repoussé : la disparition de Google Assistant sur mobile était initialement prévue en 2025, avant d’être reportée à 2026. Le déploiement a commencé début septembre et s’est étalé sur plusieurs semaines. Pour les personnes habituées à revenir à l’ancien outil lorsqu’une commande ne fonctionnait pas comme prévu, cette solution de repli n’est plus proposée sur les appareils migrés.
Seules les enceintes Nest gardent Assistant
La disparition de l’option concerne aussi les appareils associés au mobile : montres Wear OS, écouteurs et casques, ainsi qu’Android Auto. La distinction compte dans la voiture : Android Auto dépend d’un téléphone connecté, tandis que les véhicules équipés de Google intégré ne font pas partie de cette vague de migration.
Google Assistant reste également disponible, à ce stade, sur les enceintes et écrans Google Nest et Google Home, ainsi que sur d’autres appareils compatibles de cette catégorie. Google TV n’est pas non plus concerné par cette étape. Parler d’une extinction générale de l’ancien assistant serait donc prématuré : c’est d’abord son rôle sur le téléphone, et sur les équipements qui lui sont liés, qui prend fin.
Le passage à Gemini dépend encore du téléphone et du pays
La migration vise les appareils répondant aux exigences minimales de Gemini, dans les régions où le service est disponible : un téléphone trop ancien ou situé dans une région non prise en charge pourrait donc suivre un autre calendrier.
Google étend les capacités de Gemini aux appels, aux messages, aux minuteurs et aux interactions avec d’autres applications. Cette ambition va au-delà des commandes vocales classiques, comme le montre aussi le projet Gemini Intelligence sur Android. Elle ne démontre pas, à elle seule, que chaque geste du quotidien fonctionnera de la même manière qu’avec Assistant.
La disparition du bouton de retour rend le changement difficile à ignorer : si une commande essentielle à votre usage se comporte différemment avec Gemini, les réglages ne permettront plus de retrouver l’ancien fonctionnement sur un téléphone migré… Adieu Google Assistant.

articles.title: Sweden tells citizens to be ruder to phone scammers as criminals take advantage of good manners
articles.text:
Sweden tells citizens to be ruder to phone scammers as criminals take advantage of good manners
Go scam yourself
- Swedish celebrities are fronting a campaign to be rude to phone scammers
- The majority of Swedish phone scam victims are over 60
- Swedish police state that fraudsters collect around 5.7 billion SEK a year, over £431 million
Swedish celebrities have been hired to help the national government promote the use of profanity when dealing with telephone scammers.
The famously well-mannered Swedes are being encouraged to employ potty-mouthed responses when bothered by vishing scams and other attempts to steal money over the phone.
Swedish law enforcement states that 5.7 billion Swedish krona – £431 million or $575.3 million is stolen every year by fraudsters, many of which operate over the phone. The campaign is targeting over 60s as they are the main target for scammers.
Targeting over 60s
Christina Schollin, Claes Elfsberg, Suzanne Reuter, and Lennart Jähkel are participating in the campaign, which aims to provide elderly Swedes with the confidence to tell phone scammers to “go away” with whatever expletives come to mind.
By aiming for the over 60 demographic, the criminals perpetuating the crimes aim to leverage feelings of trust in institutions, often posing as government agencies or banks, often initiating contact via text message.
When the target calls the number in the message, the scammers employ tried-and-tested scripts to persuade the victim of the importance of their call, applying subtle stress and panic to push them into parting with their cash.
But the campaign is more than about turning Sweden into a land of sewer-minded insults -- over-60s are being educated not just in delivering a timely profanity, but also in recognizing when they are being scammed. With the new campaign, swearing is merely one option. Being confident to simply hang up, or tell a fake cop scammer to go away, are both good alternatives.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Don't be fooled
The notion of being rude to a stranger on the phone is not one that comes naturally to the Swedish people, which is why the campaign has been launched with well-known celebrities. Actress Christina Schollin, journalist Claes Elfsberg, actor Lennart Jähkel, are three of the famous faces, and all have one thing in common; like the key demographic of scam victims, they are over 60.
Swedish comedian and actress Suzanne Reuter is the first to feature, and says "I'm in the police campaign because it's a terrible crime that affects so many people. If I can use my voice to help someone not be fooled, then I want to do it. Many of us are raised to always be polite and accommodating, and there are many of my generation. But today you have to dare to be a little more questioning.”
She adds: “It's not nasty - it's self-protection.”

articles.title: "Protect Our Games" Act Aims to Save Online Games in the United States
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
	
	
	
"Protect Our Games" Act Aims to Save Online Games in the United States
According to a newly proposed bill called the "Protect Our Games Act," United States Democratic Senator John Kane has introduced an initiative aimed at preserving games and assisting consumers who already own them. We've seen countless instances where you buy a game, and then an online server gets shut down at some point, rendering your games unplayable. To prevent this, the US Senator has distributed a co-sponsorship memorandum to members of the Pennsylvania State Senate, who plan to propose the new "Protect Our Games Act" to the United States Senate with participation from all 50 states. While it is not yet a proposed bill, it is shaping up to be one of the most impactful acts the government could impose. After failing in California, Pennsylvania might be the next state to push it.
Specifically, the proposal states that game developers would be required to inform their customers at least 60 days in advance of any intention to discontinue the game or make changes affecting its functionality, such as shutting down online servers. If such changes are necessary, game developers would need to offer one of three proposed options. The first option is to keep the game playable offline. The second option requires developers to provide a patch that allows continued online use independent of the developer's servers. The third and final option is a refund for the game. For this third option, the refund must be tied to the highest price the game developer offered the game at within the 12 months prior to ceasing operations. Additionally, the refund may not be less than 25% of the original game listing.Excluded from this act are subscriptions and games that don't require an internet connection to be played. True offline games, while rare these days, would be exempt nonetheless. Another point of interest is that subscriptions would be exempt, as customers pay for the service on a monthly basis, and ending a subscription would allow developers to cease operations without any further obligation.
The "Stop Killing Games" movement is reminiscent of this proposal, as there is a significant demand from gamers worldwide to continue playing games they paid for, on their own terms. If the new "Protect Our Games Act" reaches the Senate, it would need to be put up for a vote, compelling those serving the United States market to comply. Until then, it remains just a proposed idea.

12 Comments on "Protect Our Games" Act Aims to Save Online Games in the United States
Look what happened to Net Neutrality.
1. Companies actually do the right thing and allow separate, third party servers to run. (We all know this won't happen)
2. Game developers all quickly add mediocre single-player modes or LAN hosting. (This may happen for some games, but a lot of games simply aren't compatible with single player or LAN)
3. A massive shift to online memberships happens in the PC gaming market (It's already happened in the console market) and large amounts of dissatisfied customers appear because they want to play the game they payed for without spending additional money on memberships.
Should this bill pass, I think the most likely outcome is the latter due to massive corporate greed and a general desire to screw over consumers (Indie games are the exception here). After a short amount of time a large amount of complaints from gamers will appear and game devs will either release third party server files and remove online memberships if their profits are falling, or, continue screwing us over like Microslop has because profits keep rising. I suspect the latter in this case also.
As much as it sounds like a total jerk thing to say, I honestly hope this bill does not pass. It sounds great upon first glance, but the effect it will have on the gaming market will almost definitely be not be ideal.
We don't even know what the final bill is, but, as written, there is no chance of this passing
Stop killing games wasn't effective at doing much for game ownership, and I doubt this bill would be either, even if it did pass.

articles.title: Mozilla aposta no novo Firefox para conquistar usuários do Chrome • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Mozilla aposta no novo Firefox para conquistar usuários do Chrome
Chefe da divisão Firefox quer que navegador deixe de ser visto apenas como uma alternativa ao Chromium.
Depois de meses de desenvolvimento, a Mozilla lançou a versão redesenhada do Firefox. A mudança não só deixa o navegador mais moderno, como aumenta a sua capacidade de disputar espaço com o líder do segmento: o Google Chrome. Pelo menos é o que Ajit Varma, chefe da divisão Firefox, dá a entender.
Em entrevista ao Ars Technica, o executivo explicou que a nova fase do navegador vem para que ele seja escolhido pelos usuários não apenas por ser uma alternativa ao Chromium, mas por ter características que o tornam mais interessante que os browsers rivais.
Neste ponto, é válido fazer uma diferenciação. O Chrome é baseado no projeto de código aberto Chromium complementado com recursos acrescidos pelo Google. Entre os componentes do Chromium está o Blink, mecanismo de renderização que transforma o código-fonte de uma página web em conteúdo gráfico, visível para o usuário.
O Chromium também é a base de vários outros navegadores, como o Microsoft Edge, o Opera, o Vivaldi e o Brave. O Firefox é uma exceção, pois conta com o Gecko, um mecanismo de renderização desenvolvido pela própria Mozilla.
Na entrevista, Varma reconhece que boa parte dos usuários do Firefox usa o navegador simplesmente porque quer uma opção que não tenha o Chromium como base. Mas, com a renovação do browser, a expectativa é a de atrair mais usuários que escolhem o Firefox por suas funcionalidades. Isso porque somente uma minoria liga para ou entende o embate “Chromium x Gecko”:
E é aí que temos a oportunidade de nos diferenciar dos navegadores baseados no Chromium. Quando você observa muitos desses projetos, eles parecem muito semelhantes entre si porque é muito mais fácil criar um fork e fazer alterações superficiais do que realizar mudanças mais profundas.
Mas nós temos uma vantagem por sermos donos de toda a estrutura. Podemos, de fato, fazer mudanças mais ousadas. Acho que precisamos atender a um público mais amplo, que não se limite apenas a pessoas mais instruídas e informadas, buscando atingir um público massivo que não se importa com a diferença entre Gecko e Chromium.
Ajit Varma, chefe da divisão Firefox
Não é uma missão fácil. Em linhas gerais, o Chrome é líder em número de usuários porque as pessoas já estão acostumadas com ele, não necessariamente porque ele é o melhor do ponto de vista funcional. O objetivo da Mozilla com o novo Firefox é torná-lo atraente funcionalmente para que os usuários parem, olhem para ele e, com base nos novos atributos, decidam usá-lo.
O Firefox 157 foi lançado nesta terça-feira (29/09) trazendo um novo padrão visual. A mudança de design inclui barras, campos e botões com formas arredondadas, ajustes de espaçamento entre elementos visuais, além de novos padrões de cores e temas. É um trabalho baseado no design Project Nova.
Sobre os recursos, o novo Firefox traz de volta o modo compacto (útil para telas pequenas), mais destaque para funções de segurança ou privacidade, como VPN integrada e suporte ao padrão Manifest V2 para viabilizar bloqueadores de anúncios (o Chrome abandonou o Manifest V2), e novas opções de personalização.
A Mozilla também destaca a otimização de desempenho. Eu não notei diferença nesse aspecto, mas é preciso considerar que a nova fase do Firefox está apenas começando e, portanto, mais aprimoramentos podem chegar com as versões seguintes.

articles.title: World model startup General Intuition closes $220M investment - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
World model startup General Intuition closes $220M investment
General Intuition Inc. today announced that it has raised $220 million in funding at a $6.2 billion valuation.
The capital was provided by Valor Equity Partners, Atreides, Seven Seven Six, Point72, Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst. The investment comes a year after General Intuition spun out of video sharing startup Medal B.V.
Medal provides a free tool that consumers can use to capture and record video game footage. General Intuition uses that footage to train its artificial intelligence models.
Developers train AI models by providing them with examples of the tasks they will be expected to perform. For example, an algorithm tasked with powering a robotic arm might be given footage of robotic arms welding car parts. Manually recording such footage can be a highly time-consuming process.
General Intuition is working to ease the task. It develops world models that can generate synthetic footage for AI training projects. The company released its newest algorithm, MIRA, in June. It says the AI is more capable than earlier models in several respects.
Traditional video generators can only render clips that are a few seconds or minutes long. As a result, they can’t generate synthetic videos of long-running factory automation workflows. That limits their usefulness for robot developers.
MIRA, in contrast, can “run infinitely without diverging.” Furthermore, it’s capable of rendering complex scenes in which multiple fast-moving objects interact with one another. The ability to simulate movement is useful for tasks such as training robots to avoid collisions.
MIRA generates footage in a highly efficient manner. According to General Intuition, it can render 20 frames per second with a resolution of 720 by 576 pixels using a single B200 graphics card.
The model’s efficiency partly stems from its use of a processing approach called latent diffusion. Whereas traditional media generators process video frames, MIRA runs calculations on a data structure called a latent space. It’s a compressed representation of video frames that requires less memory. Shrinking the memory footprint of a file reduces the amount of time required to process it.
MIRA’s size also factors into its efficiency. The algorithm comprises only 5.6 billion parameters, a fraction of the number included in frontier models.
MIRA is a research demonstration rather than a commercial training data generator. In its current iteration, the model can only generate synthetic footage of a single video game. Nevertheless, General Intuition says, MIRA’s efficiency and rendering quality make it a “stepping stone to physical AI.”
The company is testing a commercial version of its technology with a limited number of customers who are working on robotics, simulation and entertainment use cases. General Institution opened a waitlist for the offering in conjunction with today’s funding announcement. The company said it will use the capital to hire more AI researchers.

articles.title: Cómo expulsar a extraños de la cuenta de WhatsApp y mantener los chats y fotos privados
articles.text:
Un acceso desconocido a la cuenta de WhatsApp puede exponer chats, archivos y fotos privadas. Por eso, la revisión diaria de los dispositivos vinculados permite detectar y expulsar accesos no autorizados antes de que otra persona lea las conversaciones desde una computadora, una tableta u otro celular.
La aplicación de Meta conserva una lista de los aparatos que tienen una sesión abierta. Controlarla requiere pocos pasos desde el celular y conviene hacerlo todos los días, en especial después de usar WhatsApp Web en una computadora ajena, compartida o de uso público.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo revisar los dispositivos conectados a WhatsApp
En los teléfonos Android y iPhone, hay que abrir WhatsApp, tocar el ícono de más opciones, representado por tres puntos verticales, y elegir “Dispositivos vinculados”. Allí aparece el listado de computadoras, navegadores, tabletas o teléfonos secundarios que mantienen acceso a la cuenta.
Cada sesión suele mostrar el tipo de dispositivo y la última actividad registrada. Esa información permite identificar si el acceso corresponde a un dispositivo propio.
Si figura un navegador, una ubicación o un horario que no coincide con los hábitos de uso, conviene tratarlo como una señal de alerta y revisar el resto de las medidas de seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
De qué forma expulsar un dispositivo desconocido conectado a WhatsApp
Para quitar el acceso a un dispositivo que no se reconoce, se debe tocar su nombre dentro de la lista y seleccionar “Cerrar sesión”. Esa acción desconecta el dispositivo elegido y corta su acceso a los chats, fotos, audios y documentos de la cuenta.
El cierre debe realizarse desde el teléfono principal, sin necesidad de tener la computadora o tableta sospechosa al alcance. Tras eliminarla, es clave volver a revisar la lista para confirmar que no haya otras sesiones activas que tampoco correspondan al usuario.
Además, al iniciar una nueva sesión en un navegador, conviene desmarcar la opción “No cerrar sesión en este navegador” antes de escanear el código QR. De esa forma, la sesión se cerrará cuando se cierre la pestaña o el navegador, una precaución útil en computadoras de trabajo, cibercafés, hoteles o casas de terceros.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué se debe activar la verificación en dos pasos en WhatsApp
La verificación en dos pasos suma una barrera de seguridad cuando alguien intenta registrar el número de teléfono en otro dispositivo. WhatsApp solicita un PIN creado por el titular de la cuenta, aparte del código que llega por mensaje durante el proceso de registro.
La función se activa desde la configuración de la aplicación, en el apartado “Cuenta”. Conviene asociar una dirección de correo para recuperar el acceso si se olvida el PIN. Ese correo debe tener una contraseña propia y distinta de la utilizada en otros servicios.
Qué datos de WhatsApp nunca se deben compartir
El código de registro de seis dígitos y el PIN de verificación en dos pasos son datos personales. Nunca deben enviarse por chat, correo, llamada telefónica o captura de pantalla, incluso si la solicitud aparenta provenir de un contacto conocido o de un supuesto representante de la plataforma.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, los correos no solicitados que incluyen un código de registro deben generar precaución. Si el usuario no pidió registrar su número en un nuevo teléfono, no debe abrir enlaces, responder mensajes ni reenviar el código. Esa situación puede indicar que alguien intenta tomar el control de la cuenta.
Cuáles controles ayudan a mantener privados los chats y las fotos
Sumado a revisar a diario los dispositivos conectados, es conveniente bloquear el teléfono con huella, reconocimiento facial o clave. Esa protección evita que una persona con acceso físico al dispositivo vincule una computadora a la cuenta sin autorización del titular.
La privacidad depende de limitar el uso de WhatsApp Web a dispositivos propios y de cerrar la sesión al terminar. La combinación de controles diarios, cierre de accesos desconocidos y protección del código de registro reduce el riesgo de que terceros revisen conversaciones y contenido multimedia privado.

articles.title: GMKtec M6 Ultra vs M5 Ultra: why the extra $50 is well worth paying
articles.text:
GMKtec M6 Ultra vs M5 Ultra: which mini PC is the better early Prime Day deal?
Two top mini PCs for the office — one clear winner
Amazon has reduced the prices of two GMKtec mini PCs for Prime Day, with both offering capable hardware in a tiny package. We've reviewed both the GMKtec M6 Ultra and the M5 Ultra - and while they're both great, there's a clear winner for us.
Best for: Anyone choosing between two capable mini PCs and wondering whether it's worth spending a little extra for newer hardware and more storage.
The deal: The GMKtec M6 Ultra is now $500 (was $700) at Amazon, while the GMKtec M5 Ultra is now down to $450 (was $600).
Why it matters: Both mini PCs scored well in our tests, but the M6 Ultra is our top choice for most users. For the extra $50, you're getting double the storage, to 1TB, while adding newer Zen 4 processing, RDNA 3 graphics, DDR5 memory, and USB4 connectivity.
This mini PC features a Ryzen 5 7640HS processor, Radeon 760M graphics, 16GB DDR5 memory, 1TB SSD, USB4, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.2, dual 2.5GbE ports and triple-display support for productivity.
This mini PC features a Ryzen 7 7730U processor, Radeon graphics, 16GB DDR4 memory, 512GB SSD, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.2, dual 2.5GbE ports, HDMI, DisplayPort and triple-display support for productivity.
Which one we'd recommend
I'd spend the extra money on the M6 Ultra. You're getting twice the SSD capacity, newer Zen 4 processing and RDNA 3 graphics, DDR5 memory and USB4 connectivity, making it comfortably the better machine.
It combines an AMD Ryzen 5 7640HS processor with Radeon 760M integrated graphics, 16GB of dual-channel DDR5-4800 memory and a 1TB SSD. Its six-core, 12-thread processor can boost to 5.0GHz, while the RDNA 3 GPU has eight graphics cores running at up to 2600MHz.
In his 4.5-star review, our expert Alastair said the "mid-level specification of this machine is directly aimed at everyday users who need a powerful machine. The M6 Ultra not only performs well for office tasks but can also take that extra step up to multimedia creation, media playback, and a touch of gaming."
The M5 Ultra shouldn't be dismissed simply because it's the cheaper machine. Its Ryzen 7 7730U actually gives you eight cores and 16 threads, alongside 16GB of memory, but it's based on an older CPU architecture and uses DDR4 rather than DDR5. Its integrated Vega graphics are older, too.
In his 4-star review, our expert Mark said the M5 Ultra was a "jack-of-all-trades but a master of none." He added, "those who are interested in its features, and perhaps less concerned with raw performance, might find the GMKtec M5 Ultra an interesting proposition."
Both machines are upgradeable, although the M6 supports up to 128GB of DDR5 memory, compared with 64GB of DDR4 in the M5. Both have two M.2 slots for expanding storage.
Price context & historical value
Amazon has reduced the GMKtec M6 Ultra from $699.99 to $499.97, saving you $200.02, or almost 29%. This is the lowest price we've seen it at. The M5 Ultra has dropped from $599.99 to $449.98, saving $150.01, or 25%. That makes it $49.99 cheaper than the M6 Ultra, and it's also the lowest price to date.
For more shopping options, take a look at our roundup of the best mini PCs.
Which mini PC should you buy?
✅ Buy the GMKtec M6 Ultra mini PC if...
You want the better all-round machine and don't mind spending another $49.99. The M6 Ultra gives you twice the storage with its 1TB SSD, alongside newer Zen 4 processing, Radeon 760M RDNA 3 graphics and DDR5 memory.
It's also the stronger choice for connectivity. Alongside Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.2, HDMI, DisplayPort and dual 2.5GbE, you get full-function USB4 with transfers up to 40Gbps, DisplayPort 1.4 and support for 100W USB-C PD input with compatible hardware.
✅ Buy the GMKtec M5 Ultra mini PC if...
You'd rather pay a little less and don't need the M6 Ultra's newer hardware or additional storage. The M5 Ultra is still a capable everyday computer, with an eight-core Ryzen 7 7730U, 16GB of dual-channel memory and a 512GB SSD.
You aren't giving up much in basic connectivity either. It still provides Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.2, dual 2.5GbE, HDMI and DisplayPort, while supporting three displays.

articles.text:
Windows 11 : les Pays-Bas montrent la porte à Microsoft et codent leur propre Linux
Le ministère néerlandais de l'Intérieur développe DAWO, un poste de travail souverain bâti sur NixOS, du système d'exploitation jusqu'au cloud. Huit communes l'éprouvent déjà, sur des portables réformés.
À La Haye, l'alerte a sonné début 2025. Washington sanctionne la Cour pénale internationale et, selon le site néerlandais Tweakers, qui a longuement interrogé les développeurs du projet, Microsoft aurait alors privé le procureur Karim Khan de sa messagerie. L'éditeur conteste cette version. Au ministère de l'Intérieur, une question s'est imposée malgré tout : que pèse un État dont les outils quotidiens dépendent du bon vouloir d'une capitale étrangère ?
DAWO, un bureau Linux souverain pour les fonctionnaires néerlandais
L'acronyme désigne le Digitaal Autonome Werkomgeving Overheid, "environnement de travail numérique autonome de l'administration", piloté par le ministère de l'Intérieur et des Relations au sein du Royaume (BZK).
Son cœur, DAWO-NixOS, repose sur une distribution née d'un gestionnaire de paquets conçu à l'université d'Utrecht. Sa configuration s'écrit comme du code : chaque poste se reproduit à l'identique, se contrôle ligne à ligne, se restaure en un clin d'œil. Pour la bureautique et les échanges, la suite MijnBureau assemble des briques du français La Suite, de l'allemand OpenDesk et de Nextcloud. Tout le code est publié sur la plateforme de l'État néerlandais.
	
L'administration néerlandaise dépend à tel point de technologies non européennes qu'elle se trouve vulnérable, entre autres, aux perturbations de ses systèmes critiques venues de l'extérieur et à la perte de contrôle de ses données.
Huit communes en test, et une Europe qui prend le large
Le pilote a démarré en avril 2026 à 's-Hertogenbosch, Zaanstad, Ede et Amsterdam, d'après le communiqué officiel. Tweakers dénombre désormais huit villes engagées. Les machines sont d'anciens portables déjà rayés des inventaires, et DAWO tourne aussi sur des PC incapables d'accueillir Windows 11. Aucun calendrier de déploiement n'existe, l'équipe espère une version 1.0 en 2027.
Amsterdam a de la compagnie. Lyon a amorcé dès juin 2025 son virage vers Linux et OnlyOffice. En octobre, Polytechnique suspendait sa migration vers Microsoft 365 sous la pression du Conseil national du logiciel libre. Le 8 avril 2026, la direction du numérique de l'État annonçait quitter Windows pour Linux et sommait chaque ministère de présenter son plan avant l'automne. Berne, enfin, teste une alternative souveraine sur 3 000 postes chargés de données sensibles.
Munich, revenue sous Windows en 2017 après plus d'une décennie sous LiMux, connaît le prix du dernier kilomètre.

articles.title: Face à Cosmos de NVIDIA, AMD mise 8,2 milliards sur la recherche en IA spatiale
articles.text:
AMD a signé un accord pour racheter World Labs, spécialiste des modèles d’IA capables de créer des environnements 3D, pour environ 8,2 milliards de dollars en actions. L’objectif : mieux anticiper les besoins des futures puces face à NVIDIA.
Ce rachat de World Labs n’est pas encore bouclé. Annoncé le 28 septembre 2026, il doit être finalisé d’ici la fin de l’année, sous réserve des autorisations nécessaires. Les deux entreprises se connaissaient déjà : elles avaient noué un partenariat consacré à l’entraînement des modèles et à l’optimisation de l’inférence, comme le rapporte TechCrunch.
Avec World Labs, AMD veut concevoir ses puces au contact des futurs modèles
World Labs travaille sur l’« intelligence spatiale » : ses modèles génèrent, reconstruisent et simulent des espaces tridimensionnels à partir de textes, d’images ou de vidéos. Son outil Marble permet déjà de créer des mondes 3D interactifs. Ces travaux intéressent notamment la simulation et l’apprentissage des robots, qui exigent de raisonner sur l’espace plutôt que de produire seulement du texte.
Pour AMD, l’intérêt dépasse donc l’ajout d’un modèle à son catalogue. Observer de près la conception et l’exécution de ces systèmes pourrait aider ses équipes à identifier plus tôt leurs besoins en mémoire, en calcul et en logiciels. C’est une piste pour orienter ses prochaines plateformes, pas la garantie qu’une puce issue de ce rapprochement arrivera rapidement sur le marché.
Fei-Fei Li rejoindra AMD si l’opération aboutit
Fondatrice de World Labs et figure de la recherche en vision par ordinateur, Fei-Fei Li doit devenir vice-présidente exécutive et directrice scientifique d’AMD. Elle sera rattachée à Lisa Su, tandis que l’équipe de World Labs continuera à travailler sur les modèles d’IA. Ce maintien de la recherche est essentiel à la logique du rachat : AMD paie aussi pour comprendre des usages encore en développement.
Les quelque 8,2 milliards de dollars seront réglés en actions AMD, et non en numéraire.Tant que les conditions de clôture ne sont pas remplies, World Labs ne fait pas partie d’AMD.
Face aux modèles Cosmos de NVIDIA, AMD achète du temps de recherche
NVIDIA dispose déjà de Cosmos, une famille de modèles de monde destinée aux applications d’IA physique. En intégrant World Labs, AMD cherche à se rapprocher des chercheurs qui développent ce type de charge de travail, alors que la concurrence ne se joue plus uniquement sur les caractéristiques des accélérateurs. Il faudra aussi fournir les outils permettant aux développeurs d’utiliser ces modèles sur ses plateformes.
L’annonce ne fixe toutefois ni calendrier de lancement, ni nouvelle offre pour les clients. À 8,2 milliards de dollars, AMD fait le pari que les enseignements de World Labs finiront par influer sur ses produits. Pour l’instant, c’est un pari de recherche, pas une riposte commerciale prête à l’emploi.
L’opération pourrait donner à AMD une meilleure lecture des besoins de l’IA spatiale. Son intérêt se vérifiera lorsque cette recherche se traduira en matériel et en logiciels que les clients pourront réellement adopter.

articles.title: NuPhy Launches NuPhyLab GitHub with 3D Models for Keyboard Accessories and Mods
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
	
	
	
NuPhy Launches NuPhyLab GitHub with 3D Models for Keyboard Accessories and Mods
It seems as though NuPhy is following in the footsteps of Keychron with its latest launch, which is a new GitHub repository, called NuPhyLab, that will host a collection of 3D models and engineering documentation for some of the brand's keyboard accessories and mods. NuPhy is starting small, initially publishing a batch of wrist wrests for its Air HE series, Field75, Gem80, Halo series, Kick75, Node Series, Nos75, and WH80 keyboards, as well as accessories for the Kick75 and Node series keyboards. Node75 accessories include several display stands, a charging stand, decorative accessories, pen holders, storage boxes, a themed keycap display base. For the Kick75, there are high- and low-profile knobs, a magnetic cover, a phone stand, keyboard trim pieces, and the keyboard's switch plate.
We wanted to create a place where we can share more resources with the community and give you guys more room to build, mod, and experiment with NuPhy stuff.
NuPhy says that it will be publishing other open-source projects in the same repository in the future, turning the repository into a source for both hardware and software projects.
We're also working on some fun open-source software projects that we'll be sharing on GitHub in the future!
NuPhy is clear in the announcement and on the GitHub page that the projects published there are not allowed to be used for commercial purposes, and any derivatives need to credit the original design and link back to the GitHub.
		
		Source:
				NuPhyLab			
	
	
	
		
	
		
We wanted to create a place where we can share more resources with the community and give you guys more room to build, mod, and experiment with NuPhy stuff.
We'll be uploading official 3D model files and six-view drawings for our wrist rests, so if you're into 3D printing or modding, feel free to download them, print them, or modify them for your own projects.
We're also working on some fun open-source software projects that we'll be sharing on GitHub in the future!
So definitely keep an eye on NuPhyLab—this won't just be a place for 3D files.
