View Original
For the most part, I only found myself scrolling through the Instax film types (glorified aspect ratios) using the winding lever, and using the six picture styles, and the flash settings, self-timer and display mode options in the sub-menu. There’s little else to experiment with, besides perhaps exposure compensation, which is buried in the menu.
You can choose whether to display the selected picture style on the LCD display (kind of like a film roll), or the live view, when composing images. I'd hardly say composition is critical though, because the lens is a wide-angle 28mm optic, meaning you can blindly point the Pal 2 in the direction of your subject and it will be in the shot.
There’s plenty to like about the design of the Instax Pal 2. It’s a highly enjoyable camera to play around with, and it earned plenty of admiring comments from other tech journalists when I was attending another event.
Fujifilm Instax Pal 2 review: Performance
- Wide-angle 28mm f/2.2 lens
- 10MP JPEGs, plus a 10-shot animation mode
- Bluetooth / Wi-Fi equipped for wireless image uploads and printing
The charming, tactile and dinky design is the major appeal of the Instax Pal 2 — you’re not buying it for its technically impressive images and high-speed performance.
Take the JPEG-only photos (up to 10MP, depending on the aspect ratio) from the tiny 1/3.06-inch sensor and 28mm f/2.2 lens. There's no getting away from the fact they're lo-fi images; they're Better than the Charmera’s, but no match for your phone’s.
Don’t expect much detail in highlights, either — they blow out with the camera’s exposure metering left to its own devices, although ±2EV exposure compensation is buried in the camera’s main menu, so it is possibly to go for dark, moody photos too.
The six color profiles are all towards the vintage end of the scale, with options for Soft, Muted, Cool, Flare, Mono and Pure (see below). If you want a punchy, vivid setting, you’re out of luck. The picture style and aspect ratio used at the time of shooting, whether that’s mini, square, wide or no border, are locked in.
Technically this is a photo-only camera, but if you turn the winding lever clockwise (instead of counter clockwise for the Instax film borders), you can enter a burst-shooting 'animation' mode that takes up to 10 photos in a sequence and then pieces them into a single stop motion-like clip (see above).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
There’s a built-in battery that's recharged through USB-C — and you’ll need to do that regularly, because battery life is poor. A combination of me playing around with the camera settings and taking around 50-75 images saw battery life depleted by three quarters, so you’ll struggle to get through a full day of shooting.
Shutter lag — the time between pressing the shutter button and the camera actually taking the photo — can get really frustrating, and it’s made worse with the LED flash active. You'll need to hold the camera steady after pressing the shutter, and hope that your subject stays still, otherwise you'll miss the shot
I had the flash mostly set to auto, and it mostly only fired in low light — this isn’t a flash-on for every photo setup, as is the case with some Instax mini cameras.
As with any wide-angle camera, but especially so with the Pal 2's small picture size, it pays to have your subject close and filling the frame to maximize the impact of the photo — this isn’t a camera for taking landscape images, in which detail will be lost.
A curiosity is that the camera limits users to 100 shots between connections to the Pal app, whether that's shooting onto the internal memory or the microSD card. This isn't an issue when shooting onto the internal memory, since there's only space for 100 shots, but I found it a frustrating and unnecessary restriction when shooting to the card.
The original Instax Pal app is also designed for the Pal 2, but at the time of writing there wasn't an update for the app, so I haven't been able to try it out with the latest camera yet. I'll update this review once I've tried wireless uploads and printing.

Should I buy the Fujifilm Instax Pal 2?
Buy it if...
You love fun, tactile, cute cameras
The Pal 2 got lots of admiring looks during my test period, and the multi-sensory controls are super-fun.
You want an Instax-like experience, but control over what you print
As a digital-only camera, you choose which photos you'd like to print through the app, or via direct wireless connection with a mini Link Instax printer. 
Don't buy it if...
You just want a cheap toy camera
At over four times the price of the Kodak Charmera, the Pal 2 is one expensive toy. 
You need a responsive camera
For me, shutter lag was the major drawback of the Pal 2 — there were many occasions when I missed a moment, or the camera shot a photo after I'd moved the camera. 
Fujifilm Instax Pal 2 review: also consider
Kodak Charmera
If you simply want a tiny lo-fi camera, and really don’t care about picture quality or app connectivity, the Charmera is a much more affordable alternative.
Read our Kodak Charmera review
Fujifilm Instax Mini Evo
Also retro-styled, the Mini Evo is a digital camera with instant printer built in, and is all-round larger, including its screen. It's a similar price to the Instax Pal 2, and so it feels like better value, but it’s not pocketable in the same way.
See our Instax Mini Evo review
How I tested the Fujifilm Instax Pal 2
- Fujifilm loaned me the black and silver version of the Instax Pal 2 for three weeks
- I kept the camera with me at all times, and took it to China for a work trip
- I've shot around 150 photos using the various picture styles and aspect ratios (Instax borders)
Instax loaned me the black-with-silver-trim version of the Pal 2 for a few weeks, during which time I’ve kept it on me as an everyday camera, and taken it to China on a work trip.
I’ve used the various picture effects, aspect ratios (Instax film types), the self-timer and the LED flash, and tried the 10-frame animation mode.
At the time of my review, the Instax Pal app wasn't updated for use with the Pal 2 (on Android, at least). I'll update this review once I've paired the camera with the app and used it properly.

He's previously worked at Amateur Photographer, for a photo accessory manufacturer and as a freelance photographer and video producer, with clients including Studio 44 and Canon. articles.title: The internet is convinced Elon Musk's xAI trolled OpenAI's 'Dots' launch | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On Tuesday, OpenAI launched a new product called Dots, an always-on AI agent with a bubbly, blobby avatar. While the colorful avatar might evoke a smile, the biggest laugh from the launch is (we imagine) being had by Elon Musk, the former OpenAI founder who left, launched competitor Grok, and unsuccessfully sued.
That’s because the domain “dot.com” belongs to Musk’s xAI, and it currently redirects to the download page for xAI’s Grok chatbot app. According to the Whois domain owner registry, that domain name was just transferred in July.
It is entirely possible that xAI bought the domain for normal domain-buying reasons. “Dot” could be a typo of “bot,” so it nabbed it to grab mistyped searches. We’ve reached out to xAI and asked. But xAI doesn’t own the “bot.com” name, nor does it own other obvious typo domains like “vot.com,” which is listed for sale.
The internet’s theory is far funnier: that Musk (or his team) pulled off a prank, getting wind of OpenAI’s new product and its name and buying the domain name.
In fact, anonymous X user and xAI watcher @birdabo (this person calls themselves “chief shitposting officer @SpaceXAI“) was first to spot the domain name in a now-viral post. Whatever the motivation, the circumstance is funny.
And as for the “dots.com” domain, a more direct fit to the product name, it currently belongs to a long-defunct company. So if a petty revenge prank was really the motivation, grabbing that name, too, would be next level.

articles.title: Après un VPN, la navigateur Opera intègre carrément une eSIM sur Android avec 3Go gratuits
articles.text:
Opera propose désormais d'acheter et de gérer une eSIM de voyage directement depuis son navigateur Android, sans passer par une autre application. Elle fonctionne dans 47 destinations, et 3 Go sont offerts à l'essai dans onze pays, dont la France.
Sur Android, le navigateur Opera embarque désormais tout ce qu'il faut pour souscrire à une eSIM de voyage. Plus besoin de télécharger une application distincte depuis le Wi-Fi hasardeux de l'aéroport.
Une eSIM qui s'installe avant le départ et ne démarre qu'à l'arrivée
Pour récupérer les 3 Go gratuits, il suffit d'ouvrir Opera pour Android, d'appuyer sur l'icône de profil en bas à droite, de choisir "eSIM" puis "Claim now" et d'indiquer le pays de destination. L'eSIM s'installe une seule fois, de préférence chez soi avec une connexion stable. Elle ne commence à décompter qu'à sa première connexion à un réseau du pays visité, et reste valable un an après l'achat. Pour un voyage en Thaïlande, en Malaisie puis à Singapour, on recharge la même eSIM à chaque étape. La recharge demande une connexion internet, mieux vaut donc la faire avant l'épuisement des données.
Évidemment, la connexion profite à tout le téléphone et n'est pas restreinte au seul navigateur Opera. Cela inclut donc les messageries, les services de cartographie et autres applications. La connexion passe en 5G quand le réseau local le permet. Notons que pour ce service eSIM, Opera a signé avec Holiday.com, une filiale de Kape Technologies détenant, entre autres, divers VPN comme Cyberghost, ExpressVPN, ou Private Internet Access.
Les 3 Go, valables trois jours, s'adressent aux utilisateurs situés aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, en Allemagne, en France, au Canada, aux Émirats arabes unis, au Brésil, aux Pays-Bas, en Norvège, en Suède et en Pologne. Aucune carte bancaire ni adresse e-mail n'est demandée. Les forfaits payants existent ensuite en 3, 5 ou 10 Go, valables 30 jours après leur activation dans le pays. Opera annonce des tarifs environ 33% moins élevés en moyenne que la concurrence. Mais bien sûr, les prix varient selon la destination et le volume de données.
Notons que l'eSIM n'est disponible ni dans Opera Mini ni dans Opera GX mobile et nécessite un téléphone Android 10 ou version ultérieure. L'éditeur norvégien explique que selon une étude de GSMA Intelligence de 2024, la moitié des consommateurs ignorent l'existence des forfaits eSIM. À peine un cinquième de ces derniers auraient déjà souscrit à un forfait data. Et parmi eux, la moitié des abonnés en auraient profité lors d'un voyage à l'étranger, personnel ou de loisirs, dans l'année écoulée.

articles.title: Access management gets a reboot as AI agents scale at Okta - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI agents spark an identity cleanup
Identity and access management is getting a second look as AI agents move from pilots into production. The rush to deploy them is exposing decades of stitched-together identity tools, integration costs and security gaps that enterprises can no longer ignore.
Security teams face pressure to let the business move fast with AI while keeping control over what agents can reach. Rather than treating that as a brand-new problem, many customers now see agentic security as an extension of identity work they have done for years, according to Jon Addison, chief revenue officer of Okta Inc.
“The power of this technology is enormous,” he said. “[Customers] want to innovate fast. They’re being put under a lot of pressure by the business to do that, but they get that to have security, they need visibility and control, and they see that as highly adjacent to problems that they’ve been solving for years with us around identity.”
Addison spoke with theCUBE Research’s Krista Case and co-host Rebecca Knight at Okta’s Oktane event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. (* Disclosure below.)
Agents push access management toward consolidation
Many enterprises built their identity stacks piece by piece, and they still spend heavily to keep point solutions talking to one another. Agents raise the stakes on that sprawl, pushing customers to modernize and consolidate before they deploy at scale, Addison noted.
“A lot of those point solutions create vulnerabilities. And so as they prepare for the agentic era, they’re doing a lot of housekeeping. They’re getting their fundamentals right,” Addison said.
Some organizations are agreeing on reference architectures before deploying agents. Others already have shadow agents in production and need urgent help establishing access management controls, according to Addison.
“It is really about efficiency and augmentation for humans and workers,” Addison said. “But there’s going to be a world where autonomous agents start to explode and we’re going to have to start thinking differently about the scale of that.”

articles.title: Certains forfaits Orange vont augmenter automatiquement, voici comment refuser
articles.text:
Orange relance la hausse automatique des tarifs. Plusieurs clients ont reçu un courrier annonçant que leur forfait mobile allait augmenter de 2 euros par mois, une hausse appliquée d’office sauf refus auprès du service client. L’opérateur revoit au même moment plusieurs frais liés à ses offres Internet, mais ce volet-là, lui, ne se conteste pas.
Deux euros de plus, contre des données pas forcément utiles
C’est Que Choisir qui a révélé l’affaire, en s’appuyant sur le cas d’Éric, abonné Orange qui a reçu un courrier annonçant que chacun de ses trois forfaits allait augmenter de 2 euros par mois. En échange, son enveloppe de data passe de 130 à 200 Go, un geste plus commercial que pratique : un utilisateur consomme en moyenne 18 Go par mois, selon les derniers chiffres de l’Arcep.
Contrairement aux frais fixes, cette hausse n’est pas irréversible et l’abonné peut la refuser en contactant le service client, ce qu’Éric a fait. Sans démarche de sa part, l’augmentation aurait été appliquée automatiquement.
Un mail bien fait, un principe qui reste discutable
Nous avons nous-mêmes reçu ce mail chez 01net, pour un forfait Série Spéciale 130Go 5G. Il faut reconnaître qu’il est plutôt bien conçu : il détaille clairement la hausse, une date limite pour la refuser (le 12 octobre dans notre cas, pour un mail reçu le 9 septembre, soit plus d’un mois pour faire connaître son avis), et même un filet de rattrapage, la possibilité de revenir à l’ancien forfait pendant 12 mois après le changement. Intitulé « Information importante : votre forfait mobile évolue », il ne laisse que peu de place au doute quant à son importance et ne devrait pas passer inaperçu à moins de disposer d’une solution de tri automatique.
Le fond du problème reste ailleurs. C’est l’automaticité elle-même qui pose question : plutôt que de proposer la hausse et laisser l’abonné l’accepter, Orange l’applique par défaut et reporte la charge du refus sur le client. Une mécanique qui profite mécaniquement de l’inattention d’une partie des abonnés, même quand l’information est, comme ici, correctement communiquée.
Avant d’accepter, un tour dans l’espace client peut s’imposer
Autre réflexe utile avant de laisser filer la hausse : vérifier dans son espace client si une offre plus avantageuse n’est pas disponible. Dans notre cas, le mail annonçait un forfait à 21,99 euros après hausse, pour 200 Go de data dont 50 Go utilisables en Europe, avec la 5G+. Un tour dans l’espace client a permis de repérer un forfait « Série spéciale » à 13,99 euros, avec 110 Go utilisables aussi bien en France que depuis l’Europe. Ce type d’offre reste toutefois souvent réservé ou remisé pour les clients disposant déjà d’une Livebox ou d’une offre Open chez Orange, un point à vérifier au cas par cas plutôt qu’une garantie pour tous les abonnés.
Une pratique légale, mais que l’on pensait oubliée
Sollicité par Que Choisir, Orange n’a donné aucune explication sur ces hausses. L’association avance deux pistes : l’inflation dans l’énergie, qui pèse sur les coûts d’exploitation de l’opérateur, et le rachat à venir d’une partie des activités de SFR, Orange pouvant préférer augmenter ses prix discrètement avant la fusion plutôt qu’après.
Cette pratique reste légale. L’article L. 224-33 du Code de la consommation autorise les opérateurs à modifier unilatéralement leurs contrats, à condition de prévenir les abonnés par courrier ou courriel au moins un mois à l’avance, et de leur laisser la possibilité de résilier sans frais pendant les quatre mois suivant la notification.
Comment refuser la hausse de votre forfait ?
Si vous recevez ce type de courrier ou de mail d’Orange, une date limite de refus est généralement précisée, souvent un bon mois avant la bascule effective. Passé ce délai, la hausse s’applique automatiquement. Vous pouvez la refuser directement depuis votre espace client ou l’application Orange et moi, ou en contactant le service client. Certaines offres, comme la Série Spéciale, permettent aussi de revenir en arrière pendant plusieurs mois après le changement. Vous pouvez enfin résilier sans frais pendant les quatre mois suivant la notification, comme le prévoit la loi pour toute modification unilatérale de ce type.
La note grimpe aussi pour les box Internet
En parallèle, Orange revoit à la hausse plusieurs frais liés à ses offres fixes, des changements que nous avions déjà détaillés fin août. Pour résumer, les frais de résiliation passent à 69 euros, contre 50 ou 60 euros jusque-là, tandis que l’envoi d’une Livebox ou d’un décodeur hors panne coûte désormais 10 euros. Par ailleurs, les pénalités en cas de matériel non restitué grimpent nettement, jusqu’à 300 euros pour une Livebox 6 ou plus récente.

articles.title: Freshworks Co-Founder Girish Mathrubootham turns film producer for Tamil sports drama 'Sarpatta Parambarai 2'
articles.text:
Freshworks Co-Founder Girish Mathrubootham turns film producer for Tamil sports drama 'Sarpatta Parambarai 2'
Freshworks co-founder Girish Mathrubootham has officially joined director Pa Ranjith as a co-producer for the upcoming Tamil sports-drama sequel Sarpatta Parambarai Round 2.
Freshworks Co-founder and former CEO Girish Mathrubootham has officially stepped into the spotlight of Tamil cinema, joining director Pa Ranjith as a co-producer for the much-anticipated sequel, Sarpatta Parambarai Round 2.
The announcement came after director Pa Ranjith shared the official update regarding the commencement of filming on his social media handles, with the title "The Origin of Sarpatta Parambarai begins — Sarpatta Parambarai Round 2." Official credits confirmed Mathrubootham as one of the key producers financing the project alongside Pa Ranjith and Sayeesha.
A native of Tiruchirappalli, Mathrubootham completed his early education in his hometown before pursuing an MBA in Chennai. His career began at local electronics and IT firms before he moved into software development after teaching himself Java out of a passion for the tech industry. Over the years, he honed his expertise at prominent IT and product firms like HCL, eForce, and Zoho before co-founding Freshworks in Chennai alongside his friends. Under his leadership, Freshworks saw meteoric growth, eventually listing on NASDAQ as the first Indian SaaS unicorn to go public on an American stock exchange.
A lifelong cinema enthusiast and self-proclaimed die-hard fan of Superstar Rajinikanth, Mathrubootham’s affection for Tamil movies is well documented. When Freshworks went public, he notably referred to the IPO's secret code name as "Project Superstar" and even acknowledged Rajinikanth in an official regulatory filing with a nod to the actor's moniker, "Thalaivar."
While Sarpatta Parambarai Round 2 marks his most high-profile cinematic backing to date, it is not his first venture into the film world. He previously stepped into Tamil cinema as an associate producer for the critically acclaimed Yogi Babu-starrer Mandela.
The producing venture coincides with Mathrubootham making major personal investments in his home city. He recently grabbed headlines after purchasing a luxury residential property at Boat Club Road in Chennai for Rs 211 Cr—a five-story apartment complex named 'Anitha's Apartments' spanning roughly 18,360 square feet. The purchase stands out as one of the largest high-value residential property transactions recorded in Chennai.

articles.title: El origen del dueño de Urbagestión: de tener una calle con su nombre en Astorga a levantar un discreto negocio inmobiliario
articles.text:
En Castrillo de los Polvazares, localidad de Astorga (León) que operó como municipio independiente hasta 1975 y de unos cien habitantes censados, hay una calle en pleno casco urbano que cambió de nombre. Y ese nombre es el de Ricardo Alonso Fernández.
Este abogado de 56 años es, junto a su socio y familiar Fernando Alonso Fuentes, administrador de Urbagestión, la sociedad que el miércoles 23 de septiembre ejecutó el desahucio de María del Carmen Abascal, de 87 años, del piso madrileño donde llevaba siete décadas. Y el medio iLeón acaba de documentar que Alonso, de raíces astorganas, tiene una calle a su nombre allí, en Castrillo de los Polvazares. Pero nunca se levantó un acta del pleno que lo aprobó. Se hizo sin más, al parecer.
Ricardo Alonso Fernández. Recordemos primero que el lunes 28 de septiembre, tras más de cuatro horas de reunión en la sede de la Empresa Municipal de Vivienda y Suelo (EMVS), Urbagestión aceptó que Maricarmen volviera a su casa, pero de alquiler y con nuevas condiciones que ella aún debe validar, porque sigue hospitalizada. Según Alonso, la renta rondaría el 30% de sus ingresos netos, "unos 500 euros aproximadamente".
Ese mismo día, Alonso habló por primera vez desde que estalló el caso, en El Economista, en ‘Horizonte’ (Cuatro) y ‘Espejo Público’ (Antena 3). Altavoces no han faltado. Gracias a ellos ha denunciado una campaña de acoso, un ataque informático y la necesidad de usar protección. Su empresa rechaza el término "fondo buitre" y reclama 10.000 euros al Sindicato de Inquilinas en una querella por injurias y calumnias.
El pueblo del cocido. Castrillo de los Polvazares es la pedanía más famosa de Astorga y la capital del cocido maragato, ese que se come al revés frente a uno convencional (sopa, garbanzos, verdura y carne). Allí, entre la calle Real y la de El Jardín, hay una vía con el nombre de Ricardo Alonso Fernández desde hace años. Según varias fuentes, el motivo es que dirigió con éxito un pleito de la Junta Vecinal: un recurso contencioso-administrativo contra el Ministerio de Defensa por una concesión de aguas.
El agua del Jerga. La Junta Vecinal de Castrillo de los Polvazares interpuso dicho recurso por una concesión de aguas del río Jerga, cuya agua había sido concedida a la Comandancia de Fortificaciones y Obras de la 7.ª Región Militar para abastecer al cuartel Santocildes, en Astorga.
En la pedregosa Maragatería el agua escasea, y la concesión dejaba a Castrillo con pocos recursos justo en verano, cuando el pueblo suele crecer en población por las visitas. Y aquí está lo interesante: el pueblo ganó. En 2009, el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Castilla y León dictó la sentencia definitiva y revocó la concesión. La Junta, eso sí, solicitó también la restauración del cauce y compensaciones económicas, pero estas pretensiones no fueron admitidas. La placa, apuntan fuentes vecinales, llegó en agradecimiento.
Papeleo con lagunas. La placa está ahí, pero el rastro administrativo es más difuso. Ninguna acta de los plenos del Ayuntamiento de Astorga entre 2009 y 2019 recoge el cambio de nombre. La calle sí figura en el Plan General de Ordenación Urbana de 2018, aunque hoy ni Google Maps ni el Catastro la identifican correctamente. El propio Alonso presentó alegaciones a ese plan, descartadas en la aprobación final de 2019. Al parecer, iLeón intentó contactar con su entorno jurídico y con la Junta Vecinal de Castrillo, sin respuesta.
Hijo de un cartero, Alonso visita la zona a menudo por motivos familiares. Tras pasar por un gran bufete madrileño, montó el suyo. Quienes lo conocen lo describen en términos buenos o muy buenos ("buena persona", dicen), pero coinciden en la sorpresa: ninguno conocía su actividad inmobiliaria, sólo que tenía "intereses empresariales variados".
Más empresas. Alonso, que cumplirá 57 años en diciembre, figura como administrador único de Quesería Yebra SL, con domicilio en Galende (Zamora), y como secretario no consejero de Losada Vinos de Finca, bodega del Bierzo. Una portavoz de esta última precisa que no tiene participación accionarial, que es un mero asesor legal del consejo, y admite que el caso les está salpicando.
Su socio, Fernando Alonso Fuentes, aparecía en 2017 con un 0,5% entre los fundadores de la plataforma educativa ThePower Education: 25 acciones de Powereducation SL, las mismas que otros socios minoritarios (y, al parecer, la firma no respondió a las peticiones informativas de elDiario.es).
Hace unos días contamos que ambos administradores son titulares de más de una docena de sociedades agroalimentarias e inmobiliarias, como Valnor Activos SL y Tracyma 21 SL, creadas en 2012, con domicilio social en la Avenida de Manoteras de Madrid, la misma de Urbagestión Desarrollo e Inversión SL. Ricardo Alonso aparece como administrador único de Tracyma desde diciembre de 2024 y en ninguna figuran ni empleados ni ingresos declarados.

articles.title: Stahlherstellung ohne Kohle: US-Startup entwickelt günstigeren Ofen
articles.text:
Eine Tonne „grüner“ Stahl am Tag: US-Startup entwickelt neuen Ofen – und will Emissionen senken
Die Stahlindustrie ist nicht gerade für ihre Innovationskraft bekannt. Seit Erfindung und Beginn der kommerziellen Nutzung des Verfahrens in den 1850er Jahren hat sich bei der Aufbereitung von Eisenerz kaum etwas geändert. Die meisten Stahlhersteller schmelzen festes Erz bei schwindelerregend hohen Temperaturen in Hochöfen, wo das Material mit Gasen reagiert und chemische Reaktionen auslöst, durch die Sauerstoff entfernt wird.
Anschließend wird das Material weiter veredelt, um es zu reinigen, bevor es zu Produkten wie Bewehrungsstahl oder ganzen Fahrzeugkarosserien verarbeitet wird. Der Prozess ist auf Kohle angewiesen und verursacht allein rund sieben Prozent der CO₂-Emissionen weltweit, die den Klimawandel vorantreiben – etwa genauso viel wie die Kleidungsindustrie. Die Dekarbonisierung hat sich bislang als schwierig erwiesen: Die Gewinnspannen sind mager und die Hochöfen haben eine lange Lebensdauer, was Investitionen in neue, grüne Technik schwer zu rechtfertigen macht. Dennoch arbeiten einige Startups daran.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda 40th anniversary concert confirmed for Canada
articles.text:
The Legend of Zelda‘s 40th anniversary concert is officially coming to Canada.
The tour was announced during the Zelda Nintendo Direct earlier this month, but at the time, Canadian dates weren’t listed. Now, we know that Canada, thankfully, isn’t getting left out.
Per the official concert website, the tour will come to Toronto’s Roy Thomson Hall on Oct. 21 and 22, 2027. Notably, these are the very last dates of the tour, at least at the time of writing. Unfortunately, Toronto is the only Canadian city listed, although the website mentions that additional cities may be announced in the future. (Ironically, Nintendo of Canada is based in Burnaby, B.C., with their sole Canadian studio, Luigi’s Mansion developer Next Level Games, being in Vancouver.)
It should also be noted that tickets are set to go live in several cities on Sept. 30, but the two Toronto shows still just state “on sale TBA.” We’ll update this story once that changes.
The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Concert is the series’ first official global concert tour since The Legend of Zelda Symphony of the Goddess, which ran from 2012 to 2017. That said, Nintendo did publish a sweet 30-minute orchestra performance on YouTube in 2024.
Given how much incredible music is featured in the Zelda series, this concert should be a real treat for fans. Of course, this is just one way that Nintendo is celebrating the big 40th anniversary milestone. Outside of that, the company also has a remake of Ocarina of Time coming on Nov. 5, a special edition Zelda-themed Switch 2 console coming the week prior and the live-action Zelda movie hitting theatres on April 30, 2027.

articles.title: Desde falsos descuentos hasta ofertas de trabajo que no existen: así roban dinero con códigos QR
articles.text:
Los códigos QR se consolidaron como una herramienta habitual para acceder a menús, realizar pagos, consultar promociones o seguir envíos. A la par, esa expansión abrió espacio para el quishing, una estafa que usa estos códigos para conducir a las víctimas hacia páginas falsas, formularios de captura de datos o descargas de malware.
Kaspersky advierte que los ciberdelincuentes aprovechan la apariencia cotidiana de los QR y la rapidez con la que se escanean desde un teléfono.
PUBLICIDAD
El código puede llegar por correo, mensajes de texto, redes sociales, carteles o pegatinas colocadas en lugares públicos. El objetivo suele ser el mismo: obtener datos personales, claves bancarias o dinero.
Cómo roban con falsos descuentos que prometen precios bajos
Una de las maniobras más frecuentes ofrece descuentos inexistentes en productos o servicios conocidos. Los estafadores distribuyen códigos QR que prometen rebajas importantes y los presentan como parte de una campaña comercial, una liquidación o un beneficio por tiempo limitado.
El mensaje busca que la persona actúe con rapidez y no revise el origen de la oferta. Al escanear el código, el usuario llega a un sitio que imita la estética de una tienda o plataforma de pagos.
PUBLICIDAD
Allí se solicitan datos personales, números de tarjeta y códigos de seguridad para acceder a una promoción que nunca se concreta. La pérdida puede incluir tanto el cargo por una compra ficticia como el uso posterior de la información bancaria obtenida.
Por qué las ofertas de trabajo pueden esconder un intento de fraude
Las falsas oportunidades de trabajo aprovechan la necesidad de conseguir empleo y la circulación de avisos por redes sociales, aplicaciones y correos. El anuncio suele prometer remuneraciones elevadas, tareas simples o contratación inmediata, e incluye un QR para completar una supuesta postulación.
Según Kaspersky, el código dirige a una página de phishing que pide información personal y financiera. Los formularios pueden solicitar datos de identidad, cuentas bancarias o claves con el argumento de que son necesarios para avanzar en el proceso de selección.
PUBLICIDAD
Los usuarios deben saber que una oferta laboral legítima no debería exigir pagos ni credenciales financieras para iniciar una candidatura.
De qué forma se usan códigos QR para vender entradas falsas
Los códigos QR se usan para vender entradas falsas para recitales, partidos, festivales o espectáculos. En algunos casos, los atacantes anuncian eventos inexistentes. En otros, ofrecen boletos para actividades reales, aunque no tienen autorización para comercializarlos ni cuentan con las entradas prometidas.
La víctima escanea el código con la expectativa de reservar o pagar un acceso. La página fraudulenta puede pedir datos de una tarjeta, información de contacto y documentos de identidad.
Después del pago, no llega ninguna entrada válida. El mecanismo permite a los estafadores quedarse con el dinero y reunir información que puede utilizarse en otros intentos de fraude.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo los estafadores pueden suplantar bancos y operaciones con criptomonedas
En las estafas bancarias, el QR suele aparecer en mensajes que alertan sobre un bloqueo de cuenta, un movimiento inusual o la necesidad de actualizar información. El diseño del correo o del mensaje puede reproducir el nombre y los colores de una entidad financiera, lo que refuerza la apariencia de autenticidad.
Tras el escaneo, la persona ingresa a una web falsa que solicita usuario, contraseña, códigos de verificación o datos de tarjetas. Los fraudes vinculados con criptomonedas siguen una lógica similar.
El QR aparenta iniciar una transferencia legítima, pero puede contener la dirección de una billetera controlada por el estafador. Una vez enviada, la operación suele ser difícil de revertir.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué riesgos tienen los QR en entregas y menús
Existen mensajes que simulan ser avisos de entrega de paquetes y códigos colocados sobre menús de restaurantes. En el primer caso, se presenta un supuesto seguimiento de envío; en el segundo, el QR puede reemplazar al código auténtico del local.
Ambas variantes pueden llevar a sitios que buscan información personal o intentan instalar software malicioso en el dispositivo. La forma de prevenir riesgos general es revisar la dirección web antes de ingresar datos, evitar escanear códigos recibidos desde remitentes desconocidos.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Claude en panne ce 29 septembre : des centaines de signalements et plusieurs services touchés
articles.text:
Claude en panne ce 29 septembre : des centaines de signalements et plusieurs services touchés
Claude connaît une importante vague de dysfonctionnements ce mardi 29 septembre 2026 en France. Anthropic confirme des erreurs sur Claude.ai, ses applications mobiles et desktop, Claude Code et Claude Cowork, tandis que les signalements explosent sur Downdetector.
Depuis la fin de l’après-midi, de nombreuses personnes rencontrent des difficultés pour accéder à Claude ou poursuivre leurs conversations. Les témoignages concordent avec l’alerte publiée par Anthropic : requêtes qui échouent, conversations impossibles à charger ou à envoyer, voire demandes répétées de reconnexion.
La courbe de Downdetector montre une hausse particulièrement brutale. Après être resté proche de son niveau habituel pendant plusieurs heures, le nombre de signalements bondit peu après 16 heures pour atteindre 727 à 16 h 06. Ce chiffre mesure les déclarations reçues par la plateforme et ne permet donc pas d’établir le nombre total de personnes touchées.
Claude.ai, Claude Code et Claude Cowork sont concernés
Anthropic a officiellement reconnu l’incident le 29 septembre 2026 à 14 h 21 UTC, soit 16 h 21 en France métropolitaine.
Selon l’entreprise, les perturbations affectent Claude.ai, y compris ses applications pour ordinateur et mobile, ainsi que Claude Code et Claude Cowork. Les abonnés peuvent rencontrer des échecs lors de l’envoi de leurs demandes ou du chargement de leurs conversations. Une nouvelle tentative peut parfois aboutir.
L’ampleur exacte de la panne reste inconnue à ce stade et aucun délai de rétablissement n’a été annoncé.

articles.title: OpenAI makes 'Sign in with ChatGPT' a way to use your subscription in third-party developer tools
articles.text:
OpenAI makes ‘Sign in with ChatGPT’ a way to use your subscription in third-party developer tools
OpenAI has announced that it’s making it easier for ChatGPT subscribers to use their allowance inside third-party AI and coding platforms such as Amp, Devin, Lovable, and OpenClaw, alongside broader developer and productivity platforms including Notion and Vercel.
The announcement came on Tuesday at OpenAI DevDay, the fourth incarnation of its annual developer conference, where the AI juggernaut unveiled a number of notable tidbits, including Dots, a new class of always-on agents, and GPT-6.1 Sol, its latest model for coding, computer use and professional work.
Speaking on stage, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told developers that enabling users to bring their existing ChatGPT allowance into their products could lower the barrier to adoption for those tools.
“This makes it easier for people to try your product,” Altman said. “They’re already paying for an AI subscription, and now you don’t have to cover their token costs to get them going.”
Sign in with ChatGPT: Identity and plan usage
Back in July, OpenAI had already released Sign in with ChatGPT as a beta feature in partnership with companies including Airtable, GitLab, HubSpot, Notion, Supabase, and Vercel.
At that point, however, the feature was chiefly about identity. Users could create or access an account on participating sites using their ChatGPT login, while supported plugins could use the same sign-in process to create or link an account with the underlying service.
OpenAI DevDay 2026 coverage:
OpenAI said partners received a user’s name, email address and profile picture, while any additional plugin permissions had to be approved separately.
Now, OpenAI is extending that idea beyond identity, allowing ChatGPT Plus and Pro subscribers to use their existing plan allowance inside participating third-party tools. “Eligible” OpenAI usage in those services counts against the user’s existing ChatGPT plan limits, with controls for how much each partner can consume.
OpenAI has named 16 launch partners for ChatGPT plan usage, spanning both open-source and commercial tools. The currently available services include OpenCode, OpenClaw, Pi, T3, Hyperagent, Hermes Agent, Vorflux, Amp, Dactyl, Kilo Code, Warp, Conductor, Devin, Notion and Vercel, with Lovable “coming soon.”
An OpenAI spokesperson tells The New Stack that more will be added to the mix in the future.
“We’re starting with these 16 launch partners today, and we’ll expand quickly,” the company says in a statement.
Extending ChatGPT subscriptions
It’s worth noting that at least one of the launch partners has been showcasing this integration for the best part of a month already. Ryan Dahl, a software engineer known for Node.js, took to X in late August to debut Dactyl, a vibe-coding platform for building native mobile apps.
As part of the launch, Dahl highlighted the option to bring an existing ChatGPT subscription into Dactyl.
Dactyl offers a free plan with 100 credits a month for trying the service, while its $20-a-month Builder plan puts the ChatGPT connection front and center, promising that the “Agent runs on your ChatGPT subscription — no token bills from us.”
Dactyl’s documentation provides a little more detail, too. Connecting ChatGPT covers the agent that interprets a user’s request and writes the Swift code. Compiling the app, generating icons and images, creating 3D assets and publishing continue to consume Dactyl credits. Users don’t need to supply an OpenAI API key: authentication happens through their normal ChatGPT account.
At the time, Dactyl said plan sharing was limited to personal ChatGPT Pro subscribers on its Builder plan or higher. Plus and Business users could still sign in with ChatGPT, but that only provided the account connection; their Dactyl builds continued to consume Dactyl credits rather than drawing on their ChatGPT allowance.
The official announcement from OpenAI today broadens plan usage to both Plus and Pro subscribers.
OpenAI says third-party requests draw from the ChatGPT Work and Codex usage already included in a subscriber’s plan. Users can set weekly caps for individual apps, and once the relevant limit is reached, included usage stops rather than automatically switching to the third party’s own billing.
Dactyl, for what it’s worth, wasn’t the first third-party tool to let users draw on an existing ChatGPT subscription for OpenAI-powered usage. In practice, that meant a service could use a user’s existing ChatGPT/Codex entitlement for model usage, rather than requiring them to pay separately through the OpenAI API or the service’s own credits.
OpenClaw was one example of this in operation. In May, it announced that users could power OpenAI agent turns with their existing ChatGPT subscription through OpenAI’s Codex authentication route. Users signed into their ChatGPT/Codex account from the OpenClaw command line, creating what OpenClaw called a “subscription-backed Codex auth profile.”
And so today’s launch brings those various implementations into a wider program that users can manage directly through ChatGPT.
“Today’s rollout builds on that earlier work, bringing plan usage to more participating tools with clearer visibility and controls in ChatGPT settings,” the OpenAI spokesperson says.
Portable ChatGPT subscriptions
The distinction between that earlier approach and today’s announcement is also now included in OpenClaw’s own documentation. It lists Codex account login and the new Sign in with ChatGPT option as separate authentication methods, alongside a traditional OpenAI API key. Sign in with ChatGPT is specifically described as using a user’s Codex allowance with its own usage tracking and token limits.
And this also helps illustrate what OpenAI is adding today. A ChatGPT subscription and OpenAI’s developer API have traditionally been separate products: developers using OpenAI through its API generally supply an API key and pay according to usage, while third-party services may instead pass those model costs on through their own subscriptions or credit systems.
Sign in with ChatGPT gives participating services an official route for letting users bring their existing ChatGPT allowance with them.

articles.title: Apps e sites da Justiça Eleitoral terão acesso grátis nas Eleições • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apps e sites da Justiça Eleitoral terão acesso grátis nas Eleições
Liminar do ministro do STF Cristiano Zanin prevê navegação sem consumo de dados móveis. Medida ainda depende de votação no plenário virtual do Supremo.
Sites e aplicativos da Justiça Eleitoral terão acesso gratuito para usuários que estiverem sem dados móveis disponíveis. É o que prevê a medida cautelar assinada pelo ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) Cristiano Zanin sobre o chamado zero rating.
A decisão partiu de um requerimento da Confederação Nacional dos Trabalhadores em Educação (CNTE) e de uma sugestão da Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) junto à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), conforme o Tecnoblog noticiou na semana passada.
Esse pedido foi parcialmente acatado pelo ministro Zanin. Com a decisão, qualquer brasileiro poderá checar informações sobre o processo eleitoral em plataformas oficiais do setor sem créditos de internet no celular.
No entanto, como se trata de uma liminar, a decisão será submetida ao plenário virtual do STF nesta terça-feira (29/09). Segundo o Mobile Time, se for aprovada, a medida entrará em vigor 72 horas antes de cada turno das Eleições 2026 e permanecerá válida até 24 horas após o encerramento da votação.
Entram na medida plataformas oficiais da Justiça Eleitoral brasileira, incluindo:
O acesso a essas plataformas é considerado relevante por informarem detalhes como local de votação, dados de candidatos, além da própria apuração do pleito. A ideia é garantir que todos os eleitores possam checar essas informações durante o momento crítico da eleição. Outros endereços indicados como indispensáveis pelo TSE também entram na conta, mas não foram incluídos exemplos no documento.
Contudo, segundo a decisão do ministro, sites .gov, .leg e .mp não podem ser incluídos na gratuidade. A decisão diz que links relacionados “abrangem hospedagens de vídeo e transmissões de peso, (…) incompatível com o dimensionamento das redes descrito pela Anatel”.
Em outras palavras, uma liberação em maior escala poderia prejudicar a rede em si. Vale lembrar que a decisão do ministro Zanin foi proferida após ouvir as recomendações da Anatel, conforme noticiamos aqui no TB.
A inclusão dessas plataformas foi solicitada pelo requerente sob argumento de que “a parcela mais pobre da população dispõe de ‘uma internet limitada, que se esgota rapidamente’”, impedindo o acesso a sites e apps além dos indicados pelas operadoras contratadas.
O documento traz ainda dados da pesquisa TIC Domicílios 2025, que aponta um alto número de brasileiros que acessa a internet exclusivamente pelo celular (65%), sendo que 39% tiveram o pacote de dados esgotado ao menos uma vez nos três meses anteriores à pesquisa.
Segundo o levantamento, mais da metade (52%) desses cortes ocorrem em planos pré-pagos. A Pesquisa de Conectividade Significativa da Anatel também foi citada por apontar 66% da população com planos do tipo, o que aumenta a probabilidade de cortes na conexão durante o pleito.

articles.title: AMD acquires World Labs AI startup, upping the ante against Nvidia
articles.text:
Chipmaker AMD and world models company World Labs announced that AMD will acquire the AI company by the end of the year, pending regulatory approval. The transaction is valued at $8.2 billion.
In 2024, computer vision scientist Fei-Fei Li founded World Labs with fellow researchers Justin Johnson, Christoph Lassner, and Ben Mildenhall, with $230 million in funding, some of which came from AMD.
The company began working on new world models, which are AI models that aim to provide a useful, predictive simulation of the physical world. Competing architectures exist (earlier this year, Ars interviewed World Labs co-founder Ben Mildenhall and others in the field about exactly that), but many involve training a model on vast amounts of video data.
That was the case for Marble, World Labs’ first publicly usable tool. Marble can generate small 3D spaces using Gaussian splats. They can then be exported as 3D assets for use in film production, game development, and other applications. The company has since introduced additional models and tools with different emphasis or use cases, such as Atlas.
One use case that has justified enormous investment in the space is generating synthetic data for training robots. That’s a field where Nvidia, AMD’s direct competitor, has a strong lead. AMD has produced its own AI models before, including Micro-World, an open-source world model, but it has not produced a stack that competes with Nvidia’s Cosmos and related models and applications.

articles.title: Your car and its mobile app are probably handing over all kinds of data to tech companies | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Modern-day vehicles built with connected car technology such as WiFi and GPS collect reams of data about its owners. And that data is not staying private, according to a new study conducted by researchers at Northeastern University.
That conclusion isn’t new — there have been numerous investigations and lawsuits exposing how driving data is collected and shared with third parties, including insurance companies. What the study reveals is just how vast the problem is and how hard it is for consumers to avoid, short of not using the vehicle or its convenient features like remote start and unlock.
Researchers in partnership with Consumer Reports tested 21 late-model vehicles from 17 automakers, including GM brands Cadillac and Chevrolet as well as Ford, Lucid, Rivian, Tesla, Toyota, and more. They also examined 30 companion mobile apps to “understand the privacy implications of the connected vehicle ecosystem.” The peer-reviewed study will be published this week.
The implications aren’t great for consumers, whose data is being shared with tech companies including Adobe, ContentSquare, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Snap, and Yahoo.
Nineteen of the 21 vehicles tested sent traffic to at least one third party and seven of the 30 apps gave sensitive data such as the vehicle identification number (VIN), emails, phone numbers, and precise location to third-party companies associated with tracking and advertising.
This often went a step further with multiple forms of information being sent to the same third party, a scheme that allows advertisers and data brokers to build in-depth profiles of consumers, according to the findings. These profiles can be particularly hard for consumers to shake because they’re sold to a variety of companies including insurers and banks.
When researchers paired the companion app to the vehicle it roughly doubled the exposure to advertising and tracking companies.
The findings were shared with the different manufacturers and all of them, with the exception of Honda, shifted blame elsewhere and often to consumers, the researchers said. (Honda did respond by improving its data collection practices after learning about the findings and ordered its vendor Amplitude to deleta all geolocation data it had received.)
Consumer Reports was told by several automakers that some links in their companion apps opened outside webpages, which might include cookies that collect customer data. Regardless of how this data was collected, drivers weren’t informed.

articles.title: Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond
articles.text:
Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond
How close is AI to designing the very same chips it runs on?
In late August, Architect Labs claimed it had designed a chip that was almost entirely developed by AI, an industry-first achievement. AI is already used to optimize floorplans, placement and routing, verification, and other stages of semiconductor development. Generative AI can assist engineers with RTL code, whereas emerging agentic systems can operate electronic design automation (EDA) tools, analyze results, identify problems, modify designs, and repeat the process with increasingly less human intervention. Meanwhile, human engineers still define and develop architectures and make fundamental design decisions that determine what a chip does and how it works.
This creates a curious feedback loop. Today's AI models run on processors designed by human engineers with growing assistance from AI; those models can then help design more capable processors for the next generation of AI systems. As EDA vendors and semiconductor companies give AI control over progressively larger portions of the design process, the industry is gradually moving from humans using AI tools to design chips toward AI systems participating in the design of the hardware on which their successors will run.
Can machines indeed design machines today? Probably not. But will they be able to do so in the future? That's a big question with important ramifications — and engineers have been pondering it for longer than you might think.
A brief history of AI in chip development
Cadence, Synopsys, and Siemens EDA, all leading developers of EDA software, alongside Ansys — a leading designer of simulation software — rolled out AI-enhanced versions of their tools in the early 2020s, before the generative AI boom took the world by storm.
The first generation of AI-enhanced EDA software primarily used machine learning (ML) and reinforcement learning (RL) to tackle well-defined optimization problems. Given an existing design, a set of constraints, and particular targets, these tools could explore numerous implementation options to optimize placement and routing, and therefore power, performance, and area (PPA), while shrinking development time. Essentially, AI could find a better way to implement a design, but the design itself and its goals were still defined by engineers.
One of the key advantages of these tools was their ability to learn from previous runs and use accumulated data to guide subsequent design-space exploration, something which could reduce the number of iterations needed to meet PPA targets and, in some cases, produce results that would have required considerably more engineering time using conventional methods. Yet the autonomy of these tools is limited, as engineers define constraints, configure flows, run individual tools, analyze their output, and decide what to try next. AI accelerates or optimizes particular stages of chip development, but humans still control the overall design flow. And that's changing with newer generations.
The latest AI-enhanced EDA tools are considerably more ambitious. Generative AI can write or modify RTL and verification code, analyze reports, identify potential points of failure, and even suggest fixes. Meanwhile, emerging agentic systems can operate multiple EDA tools and execute sequences of engineering tasks with very limited human intervention. Such an agent can analyze results, modify a design or its parameters, launch another simulation or implementation run, evaluate the outcome, and repeat the process until it reaches specified targets. As a result, AI is gradually moving from optimizing individual steps inside EDA tools to automating parts of the chip development workflow itself.
From big bang to architectures
In 2023 – 2024, both Cadence and Synopsys announced that hundreds of chip designs have been completed using their AI-enhanced Cadence.ai DSO.ai/VSO.ai/TSO.ai tools. Moreover, leading high-tech companies revealed details about how they used AI to complete their projects. Yet putting Google, Nvidia, OpenAI, and Architect Labs into the same bucket is not right, as they represent different degrees of AI involvement in chip development.
Google, which was among the first high-tech giants to announce the use of AI to develop its AI accelerators, seems to be the least radical. Google's AlphaChip uses reinforcement learning mostly for physical floorplanning: it places circuit blocks and optimizes layouts, but it does not invent the entire design or the architecture itself. Google DeepMind said in 2024 that AlphaChip had been used for the previous three generations of TPUs, meaning Google was well ahead of the general EDA industry with its tools. (The company has not shared AlphaChip's progress in detail since then.)
Nvidia is more interesting because its internal AI systems tend to automate work traditionally performed by hardware engineers. The important distinction is that Nvidia trains specialized models on its own RTL, documentation, and unique accumulated engineering knowledge, something a merchant EDA vendor cannot access. This makes Nvidia an example of a chip designer that turns the engineering data behind its proprietary GPU and, more recently, AI accelerator, CPU, DPU, and network cards into training data for AI. Nonetheless, Nvidia itself draws a clear line between its automation and autonomous chip design.
OpenAI's Jalapeño is probably the strongest real-silicon example we currently have. OpenAI says AI was directly involved in implementation, design-space exploration, verification loops, and arithmetic-circuit optimization, which enabled the company to go from initial design to tapeout in nine months. At Hot Chips, OpenAI disclosed some concrete PPA advantages: Compared with human baselines, AI-assisted designs improved a BF16 multiplier by 56%, an FP4 dot-product block by 21%, and an FP32 accumulator by 10%, while reducing the area of matrix and SIMD units by 10% and 8%, respectively.
OpenAI has not said that AI invented Jalapeño's architecture, so humans have indeed remained responsible for it. But AI was extensively used to turn that architecture into silicon and optimize it ... which brings us to Architect Labs.
Indeed, Architect Labs' Redwood is qualitatively different. Two human architects defined the specification, after which Architect Labs says its AI autonomously generated and verified the logic, generated RTL, verified it, and produced firmware. To top it off, AI also assisted software development, including drivers and kernels. Meanwhile, unlike Google, Nvidia, and OpenAI, the company explicitly describes its system as one that performs machine learning co-design and says it can explore architectures, though without elaboration.
Redwood was 'produced' in under two weeks and runs billion-plus-parameter models, but there is a huge caveat: It has not been taped out. It has never actually been produced as an ASIC; the accelerator runs on an FPGA, and the claimed 3.4X performance-per-watt advantage over Nvidia's Jetson Orin Nano is based on a projected Samsung 8LPP design.
Final words
Just a few years ago, AI in semiconductor development was largely an optimization technology that helped engineers find better ways to implement designs created by humans. Today, it can generate RTL, verify designs, operate EDA tools, and even explore architectural choices, although humans still define what ultimately gets built.
We are therefore considerably closer to machines designing machines, but nowhere near the singularity quite yet. For now, chips are helping design their successors. But they aren't even close to deciding what those successors should be.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Claude was down for many — here's everything we know
articles.text:
Claude was down for many — here's everything we know
Anthropic is investigating 'elevated error rates'
If you've been trying to chat with Claude on the web, iOS, Android, or desktop and have been greeted with a "Request couldn't be processed. You can try again." message, you're not alone.
Claude, Anthropic's AI chatbot, appears to be having some issues this AM, starting shortly before 10 AM ET on September 20, 2026, with Down Detector currently showing over 2,900 reported issues as of 10:04 AM ET. I've been chatting with Claude this AM, but began getting errors shortly after 10:10 AM ET in the macOS app, and I'm subscribed to Pro.
TechRadar's Matthew Bolton has been trying to sign up for a Claude account for the past few minutes and has been met with errors, putting him in an endless loop and leaving him without access to the service.
Anthropic has actively confirmed the issue as of 10:21 AM ET on the Claude Status page, noting it's 'investigating elevated error rates affecting' Claude, Claude Cowork, and Claude Code. For what it's worth, Claude is now listed as a partial outage as well.
So, to track the ongoing issues with Claude this AM, TechRadar is spinning up a live blog, so follow along.
Anthropic's confirmed an active issue with Claude
About 20 minutes or so after we saw reports on Down Detector of a spike with Claude and encountered our own issues using the AI chatbot, Anthropic has confirmed an active issue. And it's a similar one that's been written in the past.
Right now, Anthropic is "investigating elevated error rates affecting Claude.ai (including the desktop and mobile apps), Claude Code and Claude Cowork." That makes sense, given the errors we've seen Claude respond with. There is no estimated time for a fix, but here's the full statement:
"Investigating - We are investigating elevated error rates affecting Claude.ai (including the desktop and mobile apps), Claude Code and Claude Cowork. Users may see failed requests, errors loading or sending conversations, or be asked to sign in again; retrying may succeed. We will provide an update as soon as possible."
Over 11,800 reports on Down Detector
As of 10:17AM ET, the latest update on Down Detector shows over 11,800 reports of issues with Claude AI. That's likely presenting itself as 'Try Again' messages when signed in and trying to chat with Claude, but also presenting issues if you're trying to sign in to the service or are trying to create an account.
Here's a look at Claude's Status page, which, to Anthropic's credit, is doing a solid job of updating these and being proactive with its statement at the top of the page. Nearly all of Anthropic's products, except Claude for Government, are seeing issues right now.
Anthropic has begun rolling out a fix
Anthropic is normally pretty quick to communicate about Claude outages, at least considering the previous ones in 2026, and as of 10:41 AM ET, it has rolled out a partial fix.
Writing, "We have applied a mitigation and error rates have dropped substantially. Some sign-in attempts, account actions and Claude Code and Cowork sessions are still failing. We are continuing to work on a full fix."
And nearly in lockstep, reports on Down Detector are starting to drop, currently hovering in the mid-7,000s of reported issues. While Claude still isn't responding on mobile, it's back to responding to my queries on the Mac desktop app.
There are still issues impacting sign-ins overall and with Cowork or Code sessions within Claude. Let us know in the comments below if Claude is responding for you again.
Let's take a look at reports on Down Detector — Claude AI is currently at 3,371 reports, a steep drop from the over 11,800 reports the platform saw about an hour ago.
Anthropic says 'existing conversations are mostly working again' with Claude, but other issues remain
Alright, Anthropic just issued a big update at 11 AM ET, about an hour after issues first began to spike with Claude on pretty much all platforms. The good news is that the 'elevated errors' issue is mostly resolved with the statement reading, "existing conversations are mostly working again' and that it was mitigated at 10:36 AM ET.
Still, though, other issues remain, including folks having difficulty signing into Claude, including single sign-on and sign in with Apple, voice conversations, new chats, uploading files, buying something, and Code or Cowork sessions. That's still a number of issues that likely show up as errors in existing or new chats that might otherwise go through successfully.
Anthropic's team is working on it, but they haven't shared an estimated timeline for fully restoring all of Claude's features and services yet. The full statement reads as:
"Update - The errors that began at 14:00 UTC were mitigated at 14:36 UTC, and existing conversations are mostly working again. A second issue is preventing many users from signing in (single sign-on and Sign in with Apple are unavailable), starting new chats, voice conversations and Claude Code or Cowork sessions, making purchases, and uploading files. If you're signed in, please don't sign out. We're working on a fix and will post another update within 30 minutes."
Anthropic notes 'most services have recovered'
Some good news: Anthropic says all services are operational again and have returned to normal. That also includes lingering issues beyond the main elevated error rates.
Here's the full statement: "Update - All services have been operating normally since 14:59 UTC. We are continuing to monitor."

articles.title: También hay móviles plegables reacondicionados: este de Samsung cuesta la mitad que el nuevo Z Fold8 Ultra
articles.text:
Este año 2026 está siendo el mejor año para los teléfonos plegables. Este tipo de móviles cada vez tiene más público, aunque la gran mayoría de ellos tienen un precio elevado que no está al alcance de todos los bolsillos. Hay dos formas de minimizar este problema: buscar un plegable que no sea de la generación actual y que, además, sea reacondicionado.
Ya os hemos explicado que no todos los reacondicionados merecen la pena, pero si elegimos bien, es una forma genial de ahorrar. Un ejemplo de ello lo tenemos con este Galaxy Z Fold7 de Back Market: está disponible por 875 euros, un precio bastante atractivo si tenemos en cuenta el precio del actual Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra.
Galaxy Z Fold7
Una forma más económica de tener un plegable de Samsung
Si lo que estás pensando es en hacerte con tu primer móvil plegable y te gusta este tipo de diseño, el Galaxy Z Fold7 es una muy buena opción. Como siempre os decimos, los dispositivos reacondicionados de Back Market tienen un período de garantía de 12 meses y un período de prueba gratis de 30 días, ideal para probar el teléfono, ver lo que ofrece y, si no te convence, devolverlo.
Pero, ¿el Galaxy Z Fold7 sigue mereciendo la pena en 2026? Es cierto que el nuevo modelo tiene novedades interesantes como el nuevo procesador o una batería con mayor capacidad, pero hay que tener en cuenta que este todavía tiene un precio mucho más elevado (actualmente, se encuentra disponible por casi 1.670 euros). En ese sentido, es una gran forma de pasar a un plegable de este tipo, pero por mucho menos.
Este plegable de Samsung tiene una pantalla de 8 pulgadas con 120 Hz cuando está desplegado, ideal para ver contenido multimedia, leer o jugar. Además, no le falta potencia gracias a su chip Snapdragon 8 Elite y sus 12 GB de RAM (con 256 GB de almacenamiento). Su sistema de cámaras es versátil y salió a las tiendas con siete años de actualizaciones garantizadas.
