articles.title: CoinSwitch turns profitable in FY26 on adjusted EBITDA as revenue jumps 150%
articles.text:
CoinSwitch turns profitable in FY26 on adjusted EBITDA as revenue jumps 150%
The company’s revenue growth significantly outpaced the expansion of its cost base, driven by strong operating leverage and disciplined scaling.
Crypto investing and trading platform CoinSwitch turned profitable on an adjusted EBITDA basis in FY26, delivering a sharp improvement in operating performance as revenue surged 150% year-on-year to Rs 324.19 crore.
Adjusted EBITDA increased more than 50-fold to Rs 86.38 crore from Rs 1.65 crore in FY25, while the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded sharply to 27% from 1% in the previous fiscal.
According to the company, revenue growth significantly outpaced the expansion of its cost base. CoinSwitch’s revenue increased by Rs 194.49 crore during FY26, while operating costs rose by 37% to Rs 270.07 crore compared to the previous year.
Revenue grew more than four times faster than operating costs, creating significant operating leverage and enabling a substantially larger share of incremental revenue to translate directly into operating profitability.
The company’s cost increase remained markedly lower than its overall revenue growth. Revenue per employee more than doubled in FY26, even as the employee base grew 11%, reflecting disciplined scaling and stronger operating efficiency across its operations.
"Nine years of building a company teaches you that growth is only one part of the story. The harder part is building a business that can scale without losing discipline," said Ashish Singhal, Co-founder, CoinSwitch.
"In FY26, we grew revenue 150% while operating costs grew 37%. That is something I am particularly proud of because it reflects the choices we have made as a team over the years—where we invest, where we stay lean, and what we stay focused on. We have built a much stronger business today than we had a year ago, and we are going into the next phase with a lot more confidence in what we can build," Singhal added.
CoinSwitch continued to invest in technology, product, security, and customer experience throughout the year while maintaining tight discipline on operating expenses.
While the platform continued to expand its active user base, it also deepened its focus on educational initiatives. These programs are designed to simplify crypto for first-time investors and improve overall understanding of the asset class across its user ecosystem.

articles.title: Mozilla dévoile Firefox 157 avec une nouvelle interface
articles.text:
Firefox 157 est officiellement en cours de déploiement, avec pour principale nouveauté une nouvelle interface. Après des tests menés en version Nightly de son navigateur, Mozilla vient en effet de déployer le nouveau design de Firefox sur desktop et sur mobile.
L’identité visuelle du navigateur a été entièrement revue pour offrir une présentation plus moderne sans pour autant compromettre les performances de celui-ci. Et la bonne nouvelle, c’est que l’interface déployée sur Firefox Desktop est en parfaite cohérence avec celle déployée sur le mobile, pour garantir une expérience fluide sur l’une ou l’autre des plates-formes.
La personnalisation et le contrôle de l’IA en ligne de mire
Pour cette nouvelle mouture de Firefox, Mozilla a décidé de faire revenir le mode compact en réponse à une forte demande de la part des utilisateurs. Grâce à ce mode, qui s’ajuste automatiquement à la taille de votre écran, vous pouvez réduire la hauteur des onglets et de la barre d’outils afin de maximiser la surface d’affichage dédiée aux pages Web.
Les équipes de Mozilla ont également repensé le sélecteur de thèmes pour faciliter la recherche, l’expérimentation et l’application des nouveaux styles visuels sur le navigateur. La page d’un nouvel onglet a également été revue et permet désormais d’épingler des raccourcis vers les sites Web que vous consultez le plus souvent pour les conserver à portée de clic.
Firefox ne serait pas Firefox sans évoquer la question de la sécurité. Si l’interface visuelle du navigateur change, ses outils de sécurité, eux, restent. Vous pouvez donc toujours accéder au VPN intégré, au bloqueur de pub, ou encore à l’affichage Split View qui permet de lire côte à côte deux pages Web. Par ailleurs, Mozilla tient à vous laisser la main sur la gestion de l’IA puisque vous pouvez choisir le modèle utilisé ainsi que les informations transmises.
La mise à jour de Firefox en version 157 devrait vous être automatiquement proposée par le navigateur mais vous pouvez forcer son installation sans plus attendre en quelques clics. Pour ce faire, cliquez sur le menu principal en haut à droite et rendez-vous dans le menu Aide. Cliquez ensuite sur À propos de Firefox. Le module de mise à jour devrait rechercher, télécharger et installer automatiquement la dernière mise à jour disponible avant de vous demander de Redémarrer pour mettre à jour Firefox.

articles.title: Cómo hacer que las fotos y vídeos de tu móvil ocupen menos espacio sin perder calidad de forma notable
articles.text:
Vamos a decirte varios consejos para que las fotos de tu móvil ocupen menos sin perder calidad de imagen. Son ajustes que vas a hacer en apenas un minuto, y que te van a ayudar a ocupar menos almacenamiento interno.
Vamos a darte las explicaciones genéricas, porque luego cada móvil tendrá estos ajustes en sitios diferentes con nombres distintos. Sin embargo, casi todos deberían permitirte hacer estos cambios dentro de la configuración de su cámara.
Índice de Contenidos (5)
No necesitas el máximo de megapíxeles
Los megapíxeles de tu móvil determinan el tamaño de la fotografía que sacas. Pero claro, si no quieres empapelar la habitación de tu foto quizá no necesites sacar fotos de 64 megapíxeles. De ahí que incluso muchos móviles tienen una resolución reducida de unos 16 o 12 megapíxeles.
Lo recomendable es eso, intentar utilizar estas cantidades de megapíxeles algo inferiores, porque mantienen la calidad de las fotos reduciendo su peso en megapíxeles. El modo de máxima resolución deberías dejarlo para esas fotos específicas que de verdad necesites que tengan el máximo de tamaño, pero para las de tu día a día es suficiente con unos 16 megapíxeles. Y lo mismo pasa con el formato RAW.
Los vídeos tampoco necesitan máximo tamaño
Hoy ya tenemos cámaras de móvil capaces de grabar vídeos en 4K u 8K. ¿Pero realmente necesitas estas resoluciones? Para la mayoría de vídeos el FullHD será suficiente, los 1.080p de toda la vida.
Aquí, la recomendación es la misma que para las fotos. Para los vídeos de tu día a día es suficiente con ese FullHD, y puedes reservar el 4K para vídeos de eventos más importantes o de índole profesional.
Busca y borra fotos y vídeos duplicados
Es posible que sin querer tengas fotos o vídeos que o estén duplicados o sean prácticamente iguales. Ya sabes, esas veces en las que en vez de una foto sacas 4 del mismo sitio, y luego se van quedando ahí ocupando espacio. Por eso conviene buscar y eliminar estas imágenes, sobre todo los vídeos por ser los que más ocupan.
En los iPhone tienes una función de la app Fotos para buscar duplicidades, mientras que en Android tendrás que recurrir a aplicaciones para buscar fotos duplicadas. También te recomiendo hacer una revisión de las fotos y vídeos tras un viaje para borrar todo eso que no sea necesario, quedándote solo con las mejores fotos y vídeos.
Hay móviles con opciones de ahorro
Hay algunos móviles que tienen ajustes de ahorro de espacio en su cámara, con las que puedes hacer más eficiente el almacenamiento. Estos ajustes suelen bajar automáticamente la resolución de fotos y vídeos, o realizar otros pequeños cambios orientados a la optimización de almacenamiento sin perder demasiada calidad.
La nube y los pendrives son tus amigos
Y si tienes ya muchas fotos y vídeos en tu móvil pero no quieres perder nada, entonces tendrás que gastar un dinero extra. Lo más fácil es recurrir a algún servicio de almacenamiento en la nube, como Google Fotos o iCloud Fotos. Allí, podrás guardar todas las fotos y verlas desde cualquier dispositivo, ganando espacio extra y eliminándolas de tu móvil.
También puedes recurrir a pendrives con puerto USB tipo C, que es el conector que usas para conectar al móvil el cable de carga. Ese USB-C también permite conectar pendrives, y puedes usarlo por ejemplo para guardar ahí los vídeos, que generalmente son con diferencia los que más espacio ocupan.

articles.title: ChatGPT Pro revient à 200 dollars, avec une enveloppe de crédits divisée par deux
articles.text:
OpenAI va rouvrir les portes de son abonnement ChatGPT Pro à 200 dollars par mois. Une bonne nouvelle pour ceux qui attendaient de pouvoir souscrire à nouveau à la formule la plus généreuse du service, à un détail près : son mode de calcul change et le nouveau forfait offrira, à prix égal, nettement moins de crédits d'utilisation qu'auparavant.
La réouverture s'accompagnera toutefois d'un changement important. Tibo Sottiaux, responsable de Codex chez OpenAI, explique que l'entreprise va modifier la façon dont l'utilisation comprise dans l'abonnement est calculée. Et il ne cherche pas à dissimuler la conséquence : ramenée au prix de l'utilisation équivalente via l'API, la nouvelle enveloppe correspondra à environ la moitié de celle proposée jusqu'ici avec l'abonnement à 200 dollars.
Deux fois moins de crédits, mais pas forcément deux fois moins de travail
OpenAI défend néanmoins son choix en assurant que ses abonnés devraient pouvoir accomplir davantage de travail qu'il y a encore un mois. L'entreprise mise notamment sur les progrès réalisés dans l'efficacité de ses modèles.
L'entreprise veut donc éviter une situation assez paradoxale : maintenir artificiellement des tarifs API élevés simplement pour donner l'impression que les crédits inclus dans ses abonnements représentent une énorme valeur.
Il y a tout de même une compensation appréciable pour les utilisateurs intensifs. OpenAI promet de ne pas rétablir sur ses offres Pro la fameuse limite d'utilisation par fenêtre de cinq heures. Les abonnés pourront donc continuer à consommer leur quota hebdomadaire au rythme qu'ils souhaitent.
Et OpenAI garde manifestement quelques cartes pour faire passer la pilule. Tibo Sottiaux annonce que de nouveaux services ou fonctionnalités seront ajoutés à l'abonnement dès le 30 septembre sans décompter le moindre crédit d'utilisation. Leur nature reste pour l'instant secrète, le responsable de Codex promettant « beaucoup de grandes annonces » lors des OpenAI DevDay qui démarrent dès ce soir avec une conférence à 19h.

articles.title: The One About Matthew Perry : Le docu Netflix qui va changer votre regard sur Friends
articles.text:
Quand Friends débarque sur NBC à l’automne 1994, Chandler Bing n’est pas censé devenir la star de la bande. Sur le papier, le personnage sert surtout de contrepoint à l’histoire d’amour contrariée de Ross et Rachel et aux excentricités de Phoebe. Mais le phrasé de Matthew Perry et son sens du rythme font vite de Chandler l’auteur de certaines des répliques les plus citées de la télévision.
Attendue le 27 octobre 2026, la mini-série documentaire The One About Matthew Perry revient notamment sur cette mécanique créative. Réalisée par Mary Robertson (déjà derrière Quiet on Set, sur les abus subis par les enfants stars de Nickelodeon dans les années 1990), la série donne la parole à deux témoins des débuts : Warren Littlefield, alors président de NBC Entertainment, qui a donné son feu vert au pilote de la série Friends, et Jeff Strauss, scénariste et producteur de la première saison, qui a travaillé avec Matthew Perry à l’écriture de Chandler.
L’invention d’un style comique devenu la signature de la série
Pendant dix saisons et 236 épisodes, Chandler Bing a incarné l’anxiété des jeunes adultes des années 1990 dans Friends : la peur de l’engagement, la solitude urbaine et l’usage de l’humour comme bouclier d’autodéfense. Le documentaire promet de revenir sur la façon dont Matthew Perry a nourri le personnage de ses propres angoisses, au point d’influencer l’écriture des scénaristes de Friends.
Matthew Perry avait lui-même raconté cette histoire. Dans ses mémoires, Friends, Lovers and the Big Terrible Thing, parus le 1er novembre 2022 aux États-Unis (Friends, mes amours et cette chose terrible en français, chez Michel Lafon, le 10 novembre 2022), il revenait sur les coulisses de la série et sur son addiction, un an avant sa mort.
Ses amis de jeunesse prennent aussi la parole, dont Roger Castillo, rencontré à 17 ans à Los Angeles, qui l’a conduit en voiture à l’audition de Friends, et David Pressman, son ami depuis quarante ans. Tous deux s’expriment pour la première fois face caméra à son sujet. Sa sœur cadette, Mia Perry Bowick, devenue psychothérapeute en partie pour comprendre l’addiction de son frère, parle elle aussi de lui face caméra pour la première fois. La série puise enfin dans des photos et vidéos inédites tirées des archives de la famille Perry.
De la comédie au drame
Le documentaire ne se limite pas aux coulisses de Central Perk. Il donne également la parole à ses partenaires de plateau au cinéma et à la télévision, comme Kevin Pollak (Mon voisin le tueur) ou Nate Torrence (Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip), ainsi qu’à son ancienne compagne René Ashton. Ses proches reviennent aussi sur sa lutte, hors caméra, contre l’addiction, un combat dont il a parlé publiquement jusqu’à sa mort.
Le titre du documentaire reprend la formule des titres d’épisodes de Friends (« The One Where… », « The One With… »). Les trois épisodes seront disponibles d’un coup sur Netflix, dans le monde entier, le 27 octobre, la veille du troisième anniversaire de la mort de l’acteur. Netflix n’a pas annoncé la participation des cinq autres acteurs principaux de la série : aucun ne figure dans la liste des intervenants publiée avec la bande-annonce.

articles.title: Microsoft is rolling out Linux container support to WSL
articles.text:
Microsoft is taking Windows Subsystem for Linux beyond just running Linux distributions, as WSL Containers is now generally available.
You can get the feature by running wsl --update, and once installed, there's a new wslc.exe command-line tool.
Microsoft also includes container.exe as an alias, so you can use more familiar container commands.
"WSL containers CLI: wslc.exe to directly build, run and deploy Linux containers on Windows, or use its built-in alias container.exe to run the same familiar container commands," Microsoft explained.
There's also a WSL Containers API, which allows Windows apps to programmatically launch and interact with Linux containers.
"Access functions to run Linux containers programmatically in your native Windows apps – unlocking scenarios like running local AI workloads or using cloud-based containerized applications locally," Microsoft noted.
The general availability release adds several features that were missing during preview, including restarting containers, copying files in and out, health checks, network connect and disconnect commands, real-time container events, mount support, and configurable storage locations.
Microsoft is also bringing WSL containers to businesses
WSL Containers now integrates with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, so security teams can see process, file, and network activity inside containers and relate it back to the Windows host.
Microsoft Intune can also disable WSL Containers entirely or restrict developers to images from approved container registries.
"With container registry allow lists, administrators can define approved registries and help ensure developers only pull container images from that list, that meet organizational security and compliance requirements," Microsoft noted.
Microsoft is also working with the broader developer ecosystem.
VS Code Dev Containers can use wslc as their default driver, while Aspire and the VS Code Containers extension now support WSL Containers.
"wsl compose up" is coming next
The most requested missing feature is Docker Compose-style support, and Microsoft says it's already working on it.
"Our aim is for wsl compose up to work with your existing compose.yaml files, unchanged," Microsoft said. "We've started on this and hope to share more soon."
Microsoft is also working on WSL's underlying networking and cross-OS file performance.
The company says WSL Containers can already deliver up to 2x faster performance when accessing Windows files from Linux environments.

articles.title: La mise à jour Windows 11 26H2 permet enfin de déplacer la barre des tâches
articles.text:
Barre des tâches repositionnable, menu Démarrer personnalisable, recherche sans résultats web… après des mois d’attente, la mise à jour majeure 26H2 de Windows 11 est enfin déployée à grande échelle par Microsoft. Si certaines de ses nouveautés étaient déjà accessibles à certains utilisateurs, cette update (qui n’est d’ailleurs, au fond, qu’un paquet d’activation pour les PC ayant déjà installé les versions 24H2 et 25H2) est quoi qu’il en soit disponible.
Voici le détail des principales nouveautés officiellement instaurées dans Windows avec cette nouvelle mise à jour 26H2. Et vous allez voir, certaines d’entre elles étaient réclamées depuis des lustres par la communauté.
Personnalisation du menu Démarrer et de la barre des tâches
En tout premier lieu, le menu Démarrer profite de nouvelles options de personnalisation permettant notamment de choisir entre différentes tailles, de retirer ou non du menu la photo de profil ou le nom de votre compte, ou encore de gérer la visibilité des différentes sections individuelles de ce dernier.
Autre grosse nouveauté, attendue depuis les débuts de Windows 11 : la possibilité de changer l’emplacement de la barre des tâches, pour la repositionner sur les côtés de l’écran par exemple. Une version réduite de la barre, pensée pour gagner de la place sur les petits écrans, est aussi d’actualité.
Recherche et Explorateur de fichiers amendés
Microsoft a également remanié en profondeur la recherche au sein de Windows pour permettre à l’utilisateur de trouver plus vite ce qu’il recherche vraiment. Simplifiée, cette expérience met de côté les résultats web au profit d’une indexation plus sophistiquée des éléments réellement utilisés au quotidien. Les suggestions émanant du web ou du Microsoft Store peuvent être désactivées par l’utilisateur.
Dans le même temps, l’Explorateur de fichiers évolue aussi pour faciliter la consultation et la gestion des fichiers, sa mission première. Cela passe notamment par un affichage plus intuitif de la taille des fichiers et par une ergonomie améliorée dans l’ensemble de l’Explorateur de fichiers.
Sécurité et protection renforcées
Sur ce terrain, Microsoft mise sur une prise en charge plus étendue du dispositif Windows Hello pour les lecteurs d’empreintes digitales, mais aussi sur des améliorations apportées à son système Smart App Control pour protéger le système contre les applications non vérifiées.
Toujours plus d’IA…
Au rang des nouveautés moins attendues par les utilisateurs, on peut probablement mentionner les ajouts en termes d’IA. Microsoft explique avoir disséminé encore un peu plus d’intelligence artificielle dans son OS, notamment pour doper la recherche dans les paramètres (qui s’opère désormais en langage naturel), mais aussi pour améliorer le Narrateur, qui peut maintenant fournir plus de détails sur ce qu’il se passe à l’écran.
Les outils d’IA disposent par ailleurs de meilleurs accès via la barre des tâches et l’activité de ces derniers peut enfin être suivie plus facilement à l’aide d’un onglet dédié ajouté au gestionnaire des tâches.
Autres nouveautés
En vrac, Windows 11 26H2 enrichit également les fonctions d’accessibilité de l’OS de Microsoft (meilleures interactions vocales avec le système, meilleure reconnaissance de la voix dans les environnements bruyants, narrateur amélioré, loupe personnalisable…), ou encore ses options de partage et de collaboration entre appareils (notamment à travers une compatibilité toujours plus poussée avec les smartphones Android).
Microsoft explique aussi miser désormais sur une fonction permettant à plusieurs applications d’accéder à votre webcam en même temps, mais aussi sur de l’audio partagé entre plusieurs appareils (via Bluetooth) ou encore sur une application caméra simplifiée.
Enfin, une intégration plus profonde des services Xbox est au menu, au même titre qu’une amélioration des Widgets et de la mise en réseau, lit-on.
Pour installer Windows 11 26H2, rien de plus simple : il suffit de se rendre dans les réglages de Windows 11, puis dans l’onglet Windows Update où la mise à jour en question devrait vous attendre, prête au téléchargement.

articles.title: Estafas comunes en Roblox: generadores de Robux “gratis”, phishing y sorteos en redes sociales
articles.text:
Los usuarios de Roblox pueden ser víctimas de estafas vinculadas con Robux “gratis” si no identifican las señales de alerta. Los ciberdelincuentes aprovechan el interés por la moneda virtual de la plataforma para obtener contraseñas, datos personales, dinero o acceso a dispositivos.
ESET advirtió que los engaños adoptan múltiples formatos: sitios que prometen generar Robux, correos que imitan comunicaciones oficiales (phishing), sorteos falsos en redes sociales y tarjetas de regalo inexistentes. La prevención depende de verificar los enlaces, proteger la cuenta y evitar compartir información sensible.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué peligros esconden los generadores de Robux gratis
Los supuestos generadores de Robux suelen pedir el nombre de usuario de Roblox y prometen acreditar moneda virtual sin costo. Algunos exigen completar encuestas, descargar archivos o instalar aplicaciones antes de liberar una recompensa que nunca llega.
El objetivo puede ser tomar el control de la cuenta o recolectar información personal. Las encuestas pueden solicitar datos sin explicar su destino, mientras que los programas descargados pueden incluir código malicioso o malware.
Cómo funcionan las páginas de phishing que imitan a Roblox
El phishing comienza, en muchos casos, con un enlace recibido por correo, mensaje privado, anuncio o publicación en una red social. La víctima llega a una página que reproduce la apariencia del sitio oficial de Roblox y solicita iniciar sesión.
PUBLICIDAD
Una vez que se ingresan el usuario y la contraseña, esos datos quedan en poder de los estafadores. Las credenciales de acceso no deben escribirse fuera de los canales oficiales de Roblox, incluso si la página muestra logotipos, promociones o un diseño similar al de la plataforma.
Por qué los sorteos de redes sociales pueden ser una trampa para los usuarios
YouTube, TikTok y Discord concentran publicaciones que anuncian sorteos de miles de Robux. Quienes administran esas cuentas pueden pedir que los usuarios sigan un enlace, completen un formulario, entreguen datos de acceso o participen en una supuesta verificación.
El anuncio de un premio funciona como anzuelo para llevar a páginas maliciosas. Un sorteo legítimo no requiere contraseñas, códigos de autenticación en dos pasos ni información bancaria. Tampoco obliga a descargar programas o a actuar fuera de los mecanismos oficiales de la plataforma.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué buscan las ofertas por tiempo limitado para engañar a jugadores de Roblox
Las promociones que aseguran que los Robux estarán disponibles durante pocos minutos apelan a la urgencia. Pueden aparecer en correos, anuncios, mensajes directos o publicaciones que advierten que la oportunidad se perderá si no se actúa de inmediato.
Esa presión busca reducir la capacidad de verificación. Antes de abrir un enlace o entregar información, conviene detenerse y revisar el origen del mensaje. Las promesas muy favorables y los plazos breves son señales frecuentes de fraude, sobre todo cuando se combinan con pedidos de datos personales.
Cómo detectar una tarjeta de regalo falsa de Roblox
Otra modalidad consiste en ofrecer códigos de tarjetas de regalo a cambio de dinero, datos personales o credenciales de una cuenta. El estafador afirma que dispone de un código válido, aunque la tarjeta no existe o ya fue utilizada.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, pueden pedir el código de una tarjeta comprada por la víctima con la promesa de transferir Robux u ofrecer un beneficio mayor. Una vez compartido ese número, es difícil recuperar el saldo. Ninguna oferta relacionada con tarjetas de regalo justifica entregar claves, códigos de seguridad ni dinero a desconocidos.
Los expertos sugieren desconfiar de cualquier sitio que solicite una contraseña o una “verificación humana” fuera de la web oficial de Roblox o de un socio autorizado que pueda ser comprobado de forma independiente. Activar la autenticación en dos pasos añade una barrera ante intentos de acceso no autorizados.
Padres, madres y tutores pueden conversar con los menores sobre el valor real de los Robux y la importancia de no compartir contraseñas ni abrir enlaces sospechosos. Si una cuenta ya fue comprometida, corresponde cambiar las credenciales, revisar el correo de recuperación y los métodos de pago vinculados.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: PlayStation launches free ad-supported TV platform in Canada
articles.text:
Last month, PlayStation debuted Live TV on PS5 in the U.S., a new free ad-supported TV platform. Now, the company has expanded the rollout to Canada.
Through Live TV on PS5, Canadians can access almost 100 channels featuring movies, TV, anime, sports, news, and more from the likes of Amazon MGM Studios, Crunchyroll, NFL Channel, NHL Channel, and UFC.
View this post on Instagram
Some of the featured programming at launch includes:
- Movies — Resident Evil, The Hunger Games, The Other Guys, Ghost Rider and more, with channels like Cinevault, FilmRise Free Movies by Radial Entertainment, MovieSphere by Lionsgate and Sony One Action Hits
- TV Shows – Community, Deal or No Deal, Fear Factor, Forensic Files, Hell’s Kitchen, The Shield, The Walking Dead and Unsolved Mysteries, Dog the Bounty Hunter and more
- Anime – Death Note, Hunter x Hunter, Naruto and Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon, plus exclusive Crunchyroll channels Black Clover and Box Sets
- Sports – Sports programming from NASCAR, NFL Channel, NHL Channel, PGA Tour and UFC
- News and weather – national and international coverage
- Creator and specialty programming – Hot Ones, Idle Mode and Spotify’s The Ringer, comedy, action sports, gaming, esports, and more
- Additional programming – gaming and esports, creator-led entertainment, documentaries, podcasts, and other specialty programming, including eCLUTCH Americas (exclusive)
Live TV on PS5 is available from the Media tab on the PS dashboard. From there, you’ll need to sign in to your PlayStation account to start watching.
PlayStation says more content will be added to Live TV on PS5 over time.

articles.title: Redditor Orders One MSI RTX 5070 Ti From Walmart for $1,099, Gets Four
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Redditor Orders One MSI RTX 5070 Ti From Walmart for $1,099, Gets Four
Orders that get mixed up often tend to leave buyers with the short end of the stick. For instance, in 2025, a Micro Center customer found backpacks inside a Zotac GeForce RTX 5090 box, and another Best Buy customer reportedly got rocks instead of an ASUS TUF RTX 5080 and was initially denied a refund. This time, apparently, the order error went the other way. Reddit user deadmanwonderland_23 says they ordered a single MSI GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB from Walmart for $1,099 and received four identical cards. The card looks like MSI's Frieren Edition, which comes with a bundled blanket, and currently goes for $1,259 on MSI's website. It was already a relatively good deal at $1,099, but getting four cards really sounds too good to be true. At the price paid, the four cards add up to roughly $4,400, and there's no word on whether the buyer has told Walmart about the extras.
One plausible explanation is that someone in a Walmart warehouse mistook a carton of four cards for a single special edition package. That seems like a possibility, but the actual reason is not currently known. As of now, Walmart hasn't commented on this incident, and the only account comes from a Reddit post, so take it with a grain of salt. Retailers have often let customers keep extra units in the past, though that is usually decided case by case. Walmart has been generous with mistakes before, like when a customer managed to pick up an RTX 5070 for just $129 due to a labeling error. Either way, it's something we don't often see in a GPU market where prices just keep climbing.

articles.title: OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Sol undercuts its own Astra flagship
articles.text:
OpenAI’s new GPT-6.1 Sol undercuts its own Astra flagship
OpenAI on Tuesday launched GPT-6.1 Sol, the newest version of its workhorse model, only a week after launching GPT-6 Sol.
The company describes the new model as “an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol that nearly matches GPT-6 Astra’s intelligence on agentic coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra’s standard input and output token prices.”
Same price, near-Astra performance
Pricing for GPT-6.1 Sol remains the same as before, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input significantly discounted to $0.10 per million tokens.
GPT-6.1 Sol is now available in the API, as well as to all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. For now, though, the model isn’t available in Chat.
One new feature is that GPT-6.1 Sol will also come in an Ultrafast version in Codex, with token generation that is up to 8x faster than the standard speed.
Although its predecessor is only a week old, the updated model shows significant improvements. In virtually every benchmark OpenAI provided ahead of the announcement, the new model ranks similarly to OpenAI’s costly GPT-6 Astra flagship model, but at a significantly lower cost.
For example, on coding benchmarks, GPT-6.1 Sol scores 6.4 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Sol on DeepSWE 1.1, with results that essentially match GPT-6 Astra—but at one-fifth the cost.
In some benchmarks, the new Sol model also beats Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 (with fallbacks), which launched on the same day as GPT-6 Sol. On the GDP.pdf benchmark, for example, which tests how the models answer questions about complex PDF documents, GPT-6.1 Sol tops out around 32%, while Opus 5.5 hits about 29%. Here, too, the results are similar to GPT-6 Astra at about one-fifth the cost per task.
OpenAI DevDay 2026 coverage:
One area where GPT-6.1 Sol performs especially well is computer use. Here, the new model outperforms its predecessor by seven percentage points at maximum reasoning, at half the cost — and once again with performance in line with Astra.
Indeed, given these results, it’ll be hard to justify using Astra for most use cases.
Mixed results against Sonnet 5.5
Sadly, only a few comparison benchmarks exist for Sonnet 5.5, which was released on Monday and costs the same $2/$10 per million input/output tokens. Where benchmarks exist for both models, the results are mixed.
Sonnet 5.5 scores 71% on DeepSWE, while GPT-6.1 Sol scores about 75%. On AutomationBench, GPT-6.1 Sol scores around 36% compared to 44.7% for Sonnet 5.5, but Sol’s price per task is significantly lower ($0.30 vs. $1.14).
Fewer errors, better alignment
OpenAI also says GPT-6.1 Sol makes fewer factual errors. At low reasoning effort, the share of responses containing at least one factual error fell from 11.4 percent with GPT-6 Sol to 7.7 percent, a reduction of about 32 percent.
These results come from deliberately difficult conversations where users flagged mistakes by earlier models, and they do not represent error rates in typical use.
Given that we’re not quite pacing the frontier (yet), it’s good to see that GPT-6.1 Sol brings Sol’s alignment in line with Astra. In general, it is better at respecting user intent and safety constraints, OpenAI says, and only fails to disclose broken search tools in 2.1% of cases (instead of guessing).
In the company’s tests, the GPT-6.1 Sol-based agents also never tried to work around an automated safety reviewer’s decision to block their agents.

articles.title: Opera para Android agora tem eSIM com 3 GB grátis • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Opera para Android agora tem eSIM com 3 GB grátis
Navegador da Opera passou a integrar uma função de eSIM para uso em 47 países. Pode-se comprar pacotes de dados após o fim do período gratuito.
Não dá para negar que a Opera é especializada em implementar recursos “diferentões” em seus navegadores. O mais recente é um eSIM integrado ao Opera para Android. A novidade oferece uma franquia gratuita de 3 GB de dados via 5G e funciona em 47 países. O Brasil não está entre eles, mas, de certo modo, também é beneficiado (você já vai entender).
Um eSIM consiste em um SIM card virtual que, portanto, dispensa o uso de um chip físico para adicionar um número telefônico ao seu celular. No caso do Opera para Android, o recurso é especialmente útil para quem viaja a outros países.
A conexão à internet não fica restrita ao Opera. Apesar de a novidade ter sido integrada ao navegador e ser configurada a partir deste, o eSIM funciona para todo o celular, ou seja, qualquer aplicativo pode consumir a franquia de dados disponível.
Como já dito, o eSIM do Opera para Android oferece 3 GB de dados gratuitamente. Mas é preciso destacar que há algumas restrições. Para começar, essa franquia é válida por somente três dias após o início de seu uso.
Leve em conta também que somente usuários dos seguintes países têm acesso ao benefício gratuito: Alemanha, Brasil, Canadá, Emirados Árabes Unidos, Estados Unidos, França, Noruega, Países Baixos, Polônia, Reino Unido e Suécia.
Neste ponto, você já deve ter percebido que, se o limite de 3 GB acabar ou expirar, a Opera oferecerá pacotes de dados mediante pagamento. Há opções com 3 GB, 5 GB e 10 GB. Esses pacotes são oferecidos pela Holiday.com e os seus preços variam de país para país.
Um detalhe importante é que, durante o período gratuito de uso, não é preciso cadastrar dados como forma de pagamento e endereço de e-mail. Essas informações só serão necessárias se o usuário decidir comprar pacotes de dados. Além disso, o mesmo eSIM pode ser usado em todos os países em que o serviço está disponível.
Repare que o Brasil não está nessa lista. Isso significa que o eSIM do Opera para Android não funciona no país, pelo menos neste momento. Mas, se você residir no Brasil e estiver visitando um dos 47 países da relação, poderá usufruir da novidade, inclusive contando com os 3 GB gratuitos, como informado anteriormente.
Porém, é preciso ter um celular que tenha o Android 10 ou superior e que, claro, seja compatível com eSIM. Até o momento, não há informação sobre um recurso equivalente no Opera para iPhone.

articles.title: Intel's next-gen Nova Lake platforms pass compliance at USB and PCIe standards bodies as launch looms — PCI-SIG and USB-IF give their stamp of approval
articles.text:
Intel's next-gen Nova Lake platforms pass compliance at USB and PCIe standards bodies as launch looms — PCI-SIG and USB-IF give their stamp of approval
Setting the stage for next-generation platform.
The USB Implementers Forum now lists some of Intel's Core Ultra 400-series 'Nova Lake' platforms in its Integrators List, meaning that the products have passed applicable USB compliance and interoperability tests. The PCI-SIG Integrators List also includes Intel’s 900-series chipsets for Nova Lake-S processors. Such tests are conducted ahead of product launches to ensure interoperability and to gain the right to use the PCIe and USB logos on new products.
The USB-IF listing confirms that Intel's mobile Nova Lake-H processor (Device ID D331, D333) is compliant with the USB4 80 Gbps specification (which is not surprising, as the part is also supposed to support Thunderbolt 5). In contrast, Intel's desktop Nova Lake PCH-S chipset (Device ID 6E6E) is compliant with the USB 3.2 Gen2 standard and supports a data transfer rate of up to 20 Gbps, which is in line with unofficial information about Intel's 900-series chipsets. Meanwhile, the Integrators List lacks Intel's desktop Nova Lake processor that is expected to support USB4 (more on this later).
The choice of the products to certify first — a desktop chipset and a high-performance notebook CPU — may seem a bit odd. However, there is a good explanation for why Intel submitted these parts to the Integrators List ahead of others and why the order of such submissions for compliance testing does not matter significantly in this case.
The USB-IF has a program called Qualification by Similarity (QbS) for sufficiently similar products, under which testing one product can enable related products to be certified and added to the Integrators List with limited or no additional compliance testing. Since USB4 and USB 3.2 circuitry in different Nova Lake products is similar, Intel can submit select CPUs and chipsets for USB-IF compliance tests and then follow up with the QbS.
Meanwhile, since USB-IF certification is formally attached to a specific product name, model, and revision, differently named products are not certified automatically simply because they contain identical USB circuitry. These products must be submitted separately under QbS, after which USB-IF decides whether the differences are significant enough to require additional testing.
The PCI-SIG Integrators List has included Intel's 900-series chipset (Device 6E38-6E3F, 6E30-6E35, 6E40-6E47) for Core Ultra 400-series 'Nova Lake-S' processors since April. In early August, the company’s as-yet-unidentified processor (Device IDs D461, D465, and D467–D46A) with a PCIe 5.0 x16 root complex passed interoperability tests and was listed alongside the chipset. We cannot state with certainty that this is a desktop Nova Lake CPU, although it is reasonable to suspect that the device belongs to the desktop Core Ultra 400-series platform.
As the official launch of Intel’s Core Ultra 400-series ‘Nova Lake’ processors for desktops and laptops looms, these platforms must pass various compliance and interoperability tests administered by industry standards organizations. So far, Intel’s Nova Lake CPUs and supporting chipsets have passed interoperability tests with the PCI-SIG and USB-IF. However, in the coming weeks or months, they will likely appear on other compliance and interoperability lists as well. Intel will also eventually need various regulatory and environmental documents, depending on what exactly is being sold and where, though such documents rarely enter the public domain ahead of formal launches.

Anyway, Nova Lake's listings in PCI-SIG and USB-IF Integrators List point to Intel's preparations for the launch of new CPUs for desktops and laptops. The latest leaks point to Core Ultra 400-series launches in Q1 2027, so setting the stage for their release early next year is a natural move for Intel.

articles.title: I tested HP’s MacBook Air rival and its design is close to Apple's best laptop — but when it comes to battery life, this Windows option is unbeatable
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The HP OmniBook X 14 is another stellar laptop from the brand, bearing its hallmark quality. The thin body is quite the marvel, while the all-round performance is excellent, handling everyday tasks with aplomb. Its battery life is also remarkable, and to cap it all off, it’s reasonably priced next to its rivals. Not many 14-inch laptops offer a more complete package for less.
Reasons to buy
- +Thin and light
- +Great performance
- +Easy keyboard to type on
Reasons to avoid
- -Inconvenient ports
- -Display can be a little reflective
- -Not exactly cheap
Why you can trust TechRadar
HP OmniBook X 14: Two-minute review
HP’s new OmniBook X 14 sets out to be an ultraportable device that doesn’t skimp on performance, thanks to its slender dimensions and powerful spec.
Its steely gray colorway conveys a simple, minimalist aesthetic that hardly pushes the boat out. This is matched by the lack of accoutrements and branding.
In terms of build quality, though, the OmniBook X shines. It’s an admirable blend of solidity and portability, with its impressively thin dimensions and light weight making it easy to slip into a bag. Its overall construction easily matches up to those of the best laptops.
One disappointing aspect is the port selection. Not only are there not very many, but they have a few design and placement issues that hamper their practicality.
With the Snapdragon X Elite chip installed, my OmniBook X review unit performed well during the tasks I conducted, from working and browsing to 4K streaming and even light gaming. It stays incredibly quiet even when such high demands are made of it, too, and although certain areas heat up, temperatures are far from worrying.
The 2240 x 1400 display is, as expected, sharp and vibrant, making for a fantastic viewing experience. It can be a little reflective at times, but the brightness levels are usually sufficient to combat the worst of it. The touchscreen is impressively capable too, being responsive and surprisingly smooth to the touch compared to many other laptop examples.
The keys are very light and snappy, as well as forgivingly spaced, which makes the OmniBook X a joy to type on. However, some may bemoan the lack of dedicated navigation keys and a number pad, while the touchpad could’ve been bigger to better facilitate navigation.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Battery life is yet another area where the OmniBook X excels. It managed to last over 28 hours in our test, which is an astonishing performance and puts it top of the league, along with other esteemed endurers, such as the Asus Zenbook A14.
All this excellence comes at a cost, as you may imagine, but compared to others in its class, it represents good value, especially the base model. Naturally, the base model is a weaker machine than the one I tested, but most of the other specs remain the same, making the OmniBook X a good value pick for those after a compact do-it-all laptop.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Price & availability
- Starts from £764 (about $1,000 / AU$1,400)
- Available now with various configurations
- Good price for the spec
The OmniBook X starts from £764 and is available now. A variety of AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm processors can be optioned, as well as various RAM and storage sizes, ranging from 16GB to 32GB for the former and 512GB to 1TB for the latter.
This is a good price considering the HP OmniBook X 14’s impressive spec. Another OmniBook, the Aero 7, costs about the same, and is similarly capable in many regards, although its display isn’t quite as sharp and lacks touchscreen functionality.
Another stern rival to the HP OmniBook X 14 is the Asus Zenbook A14, which is similarly priced yet weighs even less. However, it too has a lower resolution and lacks touch input.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Specs
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Base configuration | Review configuration | 
| Price | £764 (about $1,000 / AU$1,400) | TBC | 
| CPU | Snapdragon X Plus (X1P-42-100) (3.4GHz, 8 cores) | Snapdragon X Elite (X1E-78-100) (3.4GHz, 12 cores) | 
| GPU | Qualcomm Adreno (integrated) | Qualcomm Adreno (integrated) | 
| RAM | 16GB LPDDR5x | 16GB LPDDR5x | 
| Storage | 512GB NVMe PCIe 4.0 M.2 SSD | 1TB NVMe PCIe 4.0 M.2 SSD | 
| Display | 14-inch 2.2K (2240 x 1400) LED Touchscreen, IPS, 16:10, 60Hz | 14-inch 2.2K (2240 x 1400) LED Touchscreen, IPS, 16:10, 60Hz | 
| Ports and Connectivity | 2x USB-C (Power Delivery/ DisplayPort 1.4a, 1x 10Gbps, 1x 40Gbps) 1x USB-A (10Gbps), 1x 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack; Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3 | 2x USB-C (Power Delivery/ DisplayPort 1.4a, 1x 10Gbps, 1x 40Gbps) 1x USB-A (10Gbps), 1x 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack; Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3 | 
| Battery | 59Wh | 59Wh | 
| Dimensions | 12.32 x 8.8 x 0.56in / 313 x 224 x 14mm | 12.32 x 8.8 x 0.56in / 313 x 224 x 14mm | 
| Weight | 2.97lbs / 1.35kg | 2.97lbs / 1.35kg | 
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Design
- Very thin and light
- Solid build
- Limited ports with some impractical placement
Like many in the sector, the OmniBook X has a smart but rather unremarkable appearance. The dark and dour gray finish certainly doesn’t help matters, and some edges and contours aren’t quite as smooth and sophisticated as they could be, if judged alongside the best MacBooks — the paragon of laptop forms. The rounded corners do at least help to soften this monolithic slab, though.
As with many HP laptops, the OmniBook X is built tremendously well. The materials may not feel state-of-the-art, and the base does have some flex around the keyboard area, but overall it strikes the ideal balance between sturdiness and convenience.
This is largely thanks to its ultra-thin lid and base; I don’t think I’ve seen a laptop body more slender than this. It’s also impressively light, helping the OmniBook X to rival some truly remarkable portable heroes, such as the Asus Zenbook 14.
However, physical connectivity pays the price for this leanness. There aren’t many ports on the OmniBook X: you get two USB-C ports on the left — both of which support power input external display output — and a USB-A port and a headset jack on the right.
It’s a shame that the USB-C ports aren’t split across both sides, something I usually prefer since it increases versatility for your setup and working environment. Equally impractical is the USB-A port, which utilizes a flip-down flap to fully open, as you more commonly see on laptop Ethernet ports.
I’ve rarely seen this mechanism on a USB port, though, and it merely introduces an element of needless inconvenience; other laptops as thin as the OmniBook X — such as the aforementioned Zenbook — manage to avoid such a mechanism. Also, the headset jack is quite far back, which could be a problem if your cable is on the short side.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Performance
- Versatile performance
- Excellent but slightly reflective display
- Light and snappy keyboard
3DMark: Night Raid: 21,973; Fire Strike: 4,750; Steel Nomad: 484; Solar Bay: 10,981; Solar Bay Unlimited: 11,186; Solar Bay Extreme: 1,122; Solar Bay Extreme Unlimited: 1,124
Geekbench 6.5: Multicore: 14,204; Single-core: 2,427
Cinebench R23: Multi Core: 5,595; Cinebench R24: Single Core: 65; Multi Core: 374
Crossmark: Overall: 1,352; Productivity: 1,225; Creativity: 1,495; Responsiveness: 1,345
Passmark Overall: 4,104; CPU: 15,482.1; 2D Graphics: 393.3; 3D Graphics: 3,012; Memory: 2,552.6; Disk: 26,058.3
BlackMagicDisk: Read: 2,670MB/s; Write: 2,416MB/s
HandBrake 4K to 1080p: 29.86fps
Battery Life (TechRadar movie test): 28 hours and 28 minutes
The OmniBook X is an excellent performer on many fronts, making it suitable for both work and play. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chip had no problem conducting basic productivity tasks or multi-tab browsing. It also streamed video just fine, including 4K content; I didn’t encounter arduous loading times or stuttery playback.
The OmniBook X can even handle gaming, to an extent. It even managed to run Cyberpunk 2077, albeit in a far from spectacular manner: I had to use low graphics presets without Ray Tracing, which resulted in rough visuals and some stuttering here and there, but it was playable enough for a quick fix.
Under such stress, the OmniBook X is remarkably quiet. Fan noise is noticeable but very suppressed, and while the back half of the unit — including parts of the keyboard — rises in temperature, it remains entirely within comfortable bounds.
The OmniBook X features an LED display with a somewhat unusual 2240 x 1400 resolution. This means it’s sharp and vibrant, although its lack of OLED technology means it can’t match the striking contrast levels of the best monitors and laptop displays. It can also be a little too reflective at times, although the maximum brightness is usually sufficient to counter the worst offenders.
The touchscreen is competent, with the surprising smoothness of its surface making it ideal for finger swipes and gestures, which isn’t something I can say of every laptop touchscreens I’ve used. On this front, it even rivals the best tablets. It’s a shame, though, that the display can’t fold back on itself (like those on OmniBook Flip models), so you can’t turn it upside down and prop it on a desk for tablet-style use.
However, when it comes to that other crucial input, typing, the OmniBook X is far more useful. The keys are very light with little travel, making them feel effortless and snappy. At the same time, they also provide good feedback and satisfying clickiness. They’re generously spaced, too, which certainly helped me to avoid making typos. However, with this large spacing comes a compromise to layout.
Although it still has navigation keys, many of these are integrated on the arrow keys as Fn shortcuts, which is a feasible solution, although I still would’ve preferred them to be on dedicated keys, as some other laptops manage to achieve. There’s also no dedicated number pad, although not many 14-inch laptops manage to squeeze one in, but a few do.
What’s more, despite the large amount of space below the keyboard, the touchpad disappointingly fails to make full use of it. It’s smaller than those on some other 14-inch laptops, which hampers navigation. However, I had no issues with its responsiveness, and its smooth surface, while not as silky as some others, is still sufficient for performing gestures and swipes easily. Taps and clicks are also light and responsive, yet tactile at the same time.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Battery life
- Best in class
- Real all day battery life
- Only a few rivals can match it
The OmniBook X is among the most enduring laptops in its class. When I ran a movie on a continuous loop on battery power, it managed to last over 28 hours, which is a staggering achievement.
The only other laptop I’ve tested that matches this is the Asus Zenbook A14, which logged the same time, give or take several minutes. What’s more, the OmniBook X is also quick to charge, taking about two hours to fully replenish.
Should I buy the HP OmniBook X 14?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Considering what it’s equipped with, as well as its superb portability, the OmniBook X is good value. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design | Fantastically thin and quite sturdy, but some inconvenient ports hurt practicality. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Performance | The Snapdragon Elite chip in my review unit worked wonders, handling the kind of tasks I’d expect from a workaday device — and more. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Battery Life | Easily among the best in class. I’ve only tested one other laptop that can match its longevity. | 5 / 5 | 
| Final Score | Only a few niggles besmirch this otherwise extremely capable all-round laptop. | 4.5 / 5 | 
Buy the HP OmniBook X 14 if…
You value a portable design
Not only is the OmniBook X incredibly thin and light, it’s also built quite solidly.
You want great all-round performance
Whether you’re working, streaming content, or even indulging in some light gaming, the OmniBook X can do it all.
Don't buy it if…
You want the best interface for productivity
Although there are navigation keys, they share space with the arrow keys, and the touchpad fails to maximize its allotted space.
You want to use the touchscreen often
Although the touchscreen is very effective, the display itself doesn’t rotate far enough to allow for upside-down tenting, so you can’t use it like a tablet.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Also consider
HP OmniBook 7 Aero
For a laptop equally as portable, consider another OmniBook, the 7 Aero. Like the X, we were impressed with its capable performance and slender dimensions. Also like the X, though, certain ports could be better placed, and its battery life pales in comparison.
Read our full HP OmniBook 7 Aero review
Asus Zenbook A14
Even lighter than the OmniBook X and pretty much just as thin, the Zenbook A14 is a strong alternative. It too has great performance and a satisfying keyboard, but I don’t think its display is quite as good, nor is its price as competitive.
Read our full Asus Zenbook A14 review
How I tested the HP OmniBook X 14
- Tested for several days
- Used for a variety of tasks
- Conducted comprehensive series of benchmarks
I tested the OmniBook X for several days, during which time I used it for working, general browsing, streaming 4K content, and gaming.
I also ran our series of benchmark tests for laptops, designed to assess every facet of performance. To test its battery life, I played a movie on a continuous loop while the laptop was unplugged until it shut down.
I’ve been using laptops for a long time, and have reviewed countless models, from small budget offerings to large gaming machines, and everything in between.
- First reviewed: September 2026
- Read more about how we test
Lewis Maddison is a Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He previously worked as a Staff Writer for our business section, TechRadar Pro, where he gained experience with productivity-enhancing hardware, ranging from keyboards to standing desks. His area of expertise lies in computer peripherals and audio hardware, having spent over a decade exploring the murky depths of both PC building and music production. He also revels in picking up on the finest details and niggles that ultimately make a big difference to the user experience.

articles.title: NASA has a Dragon dilemma, and there appear to be no good answers
articles.text:
A close-up view of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket vertical with the Crew Dragon spacecraft on Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida in 2021.
Credit:
SpaceX
A close-up view of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket vertical with the Crew Dragon spacecraft on Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida in 2021.
Credit:
SpaceX
For two decades, largely in service to the International Space Station, NASA has sought to foster an “economy” in low-Earth orbit.
Twenty years ago, with a program to develop private spacecraft for cargo delivery to the space station, NASA sought to “stimulate efforts within the private sector to develop and operate safe, reliable, and cost-effective commercial space transportation systems.” In recent years this has expanded to creating an entire commercial ecosystem in orbit, with transportation, space stations, manufacturing, tourism, and more, such that NASA is one of many customers in the market.
In April 2024, the space agency explicitly laid out its philosophy: “NASA supports a robust commercial space economy that advances American industry and promotes technological discovery through in-space work and research. NASA remains committed to fostering innovation and collaboration within the American space industry.”
But just two years later, there are growing questions about the viability of this. As the second space race heats up, NASA has become more interested in focusing on the lunar surface, with a robust Moon base. SpaceX has signaled it no longer wants to be in the business of flying astronauts into low-Earth orbit. Today, the grand plans for a low-Earth orbit economy, at least involving humans, appear to be going sideways.
So what happened, and why does it matter? Ars spoke with a number of industry sources, on background, to provide some answers.
Q. What precipitated this crisis?
A. In recent months, SpaceX has made it clear to NASA that it no longer wishes to fly its Crew Dragon spacecraft, or the Falcon 9 rocket, on missions to low-Earth orbit. The company has agreed to support the International Space Station until 2030. But after that, SpaceX intends to retire the spacecraft. SpaceX has told companies developing private space stations for low-Earth orbit, including Axiom Space, Voyager Space, and Vast Space, that they cannot order Crew Dragon missions for their habitats.
Q. Can NASA compel SpaceX to keep flying Dragon?
A. NASA invested $3.1 billion in the development and certification of Crew Dragon as part of the Commercial Crew Program. But SpaceX was only compelled to fly half a dozen missions. It has flown 13 missions for NASA to the space station, and will launch another one in a few days. The company had recently agreed to keep flying through the Crew-17 mission. SpaceX has therefore more than fulfilled its contract obligations to NASA.
Q. But isn’t NASA a really important customer for SpaceX?
A. It was in the past, yes. But SpaceX now derives a majority of its revenue from Starlink, and that proportion is likely to grow even more. Additionally, as part of the process of going public earlier this year, in financial filings, SpaceX made clear that it envisions a vast majority of its future revenue will come from Starlink and orbital data centers. The category of “space enabled solutions,” of which NASA is a fraction, represented approximately 1 percent of what SpaceX views as its “total addressable market.” In other words, NASA needs SpaceX more than SpaceX needs NASA. Going forward, SpaceX wants to focus on launching its own payloads—on the Starship rocket. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman recognized this reality during a news conference on Monday, saying, “I do not think it’s a secret that SpaceX intends to sunset older platforms like Falcon and Dragon as they concentrate on their next-generation capability, Starship.”
Q. What about Starship?
A. Four astronauts currently launch on Dragon. Starship could potentially bring dozens of astronauts into orbit at a time. That would be revolutionary for access to low-Earth orbit and an economy there. However, SpaceX has told NASA it is not interested in developing Starship for human launches into Earth orbit at this time. (Again, they’re focused on their own payloads). Ascent and entry of Starship, carrying humans, would raise a tangle of safety and regulatory concerns and is not a priority for the time being. NASA has no real way to compel SpaceX, and any political capital the space agency might expend on Starship is going to be focused on getting a variant of the vehicle for a “Human Landing System” as part of the Artemis Moon program rather than human launches from Earth.
Q. What’s happening with Boeing?
A. Boeing was NASA’s other partner in the Commercial Crew program. The agency has invested $5.1 billion to date in Boeing to develop the Starliner spacecraft. Despite this, Boeing has yet to fly a single operational mission to the space station. The news this week is that, despite these struggles, NASA will invest $359 million more to support the company’s efforts to fix Starliner’s propulsion system and certify the Vulcan rocket for new missions. It is NASA’s hope that Starliner can supplement astronaut missions during the remainder of the International Space Station’s lifetime, and then be available for private space station operators.
Q. Is this a good plan?
A. A lot of people don’t like it. Some critics say NASA has basically handed Boeing (not a particularly benevolent monopolist) and Starliner a monopoly on Western human spaceflight to low-Earth orbit for the next 10 or 20 years. This may effectively end any hope of a low-Earth orbit economy that involves humans in space. However, others say NASA faced few good choices. And given NASA’s extraordinary investments in Boeing to date, it would have been fiscally irresponsible to abandon Starliner now. NASA funded two companies as part of the Commercial Crew program. If one of them is walking away, it makes sense to support the remaining one, even if there are legitimate concerns about Boeing’s past performance.
Q. What else might NASA have done?
A. Some people wanted to see NASA fund a new competition, a Commercial Crew 2.0 for the 2030s. This would have brought on a competitor, probably Blue Origin but maybe also someone like Sierra Nevada or The Exploration Company, to keep price pressure on Boeing for crew transportation services. However, a new competition would ultimately have cost NASA billions of dollars, and Isaacman seems reluctant to make such an investment given all of NASA’s other priorities. Isaacman believes Boeing can meet NASA’s needs, which are something like two seats every six to nine months, to orbit. The real unknown is whether a market beyond NASA—institutional customers from Europe, the Middle East, and beyond, in addition to privately funded astronauts—could exist at Starliner’s prices.
Q. How much does a seat cost?
A. This is an important question. SpaceX’s original price per seat for early Dragon flights was approximately $55 million. For more recent missions, the price has increased to $78.8 million. (And if SpaceX were to magically decide to keep flying Dragon longer, the price would only go up). By contrast, the Starliner price to NASA is $90 million per seat during the International Space Station era. So what happens after Dragon retires? Let’s just say no one expects prices to go down. I asked Boeing Vice President John Mulholland about Starliner seat prices in the 2030s yesterday, and he replied, in part, “Obviously we want to be as competitive as possible.” But competitive with whom?
Q. What about Blue Origin?
A. The space company founded by Jeff Bezos is developing a “Space Vehicle” for astronauts to launch on the New Glenn rocket. After some of my recent reporting, sources reached out to let me know that design work is “well advanced” along with demonstration work such as cabin pressure-vessel manufacturing, extensive parachute testing, in-house thermal protection system testing, life support systems, and more. I’ve heard “no earlier than” dates of 2031 for a crew launch. But that’s probably optimistic, and if NASA and private space station operators need to book transport in the early 2030s, Starliner is probably the only option.
Russian Soyuz-FG rocket with the Soyuz TMA-12M spacecraft launches in March 2014.
Credit:
VASILY MAXIMOV/AFP via Getty Images
Russian Soyuz-FG rocket with the Soyuz TMA-12M spacecraft launches in March 2014.
Credit:
VASILY MAXIMOV/AFP via Getty Images
Q. What other vehicles are out there?
A. NASA relied on Russian Soyuz vehicles in the 2010s after the Space Shuttle retired, and before Crew Dragon came online. With Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Soyuz is off the table for private space stations. India is also developing a crewed spacecraft, Gaganyaan. But it was originally supposed to carry humans in late 2021, and the schedule has since slipped to at least 2027. And for a time Gaganyaan is likely to be used solely for Indian missions. Counting on this vehicle for private space stations seems like a stretch. NASA does have its Orion spacecraft, but the per-seat cost for its missions is likely astronomical ($500 million per seat?), and Orion is needed for lunar missions. The Exploration Company, based in Europe, has ambitious plans for a crewed spacecraft, but it likely won’t be ready until 2035. Sierra Nevada’s Dream Chaser just does not seem like it’s ever going to happen, sorry.
Q. So what’s the answer?
A. You’re probably not going to like this, but the only real hope for a significantly lower sticker price for sending humans into low-Earth orbit is Starship. If incentivized, SpaceX probably could bring this capability online by 2030 and radically reshape the market. But from all publicly available evidence, and based on private conversations, SpaceX seems unlikely to prioritize crewed ascent and reentry on Starship any time soon. Could that change? Certainly. Will it? Probably not. SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, will do what they want.
Q. So is SpaceX just being selfish, or what?
A. SpaceX is a business, and like a lot of other businesses, especially publicly traded ones, the goal is to maximize revenue. From their perspective, it makes sense to remove distractions (such as Dragon and Falcon 9) and focus on the future of the company (Starship).
One way of looking at the last 20 years of spaceflight history, and NASA’s efforts to stimulate a low-Earth orbit economy, is to view SpaceX as the exception to the rule. In some sense, an economy based on astronauts in low-Earth orbit got lucky that SpaceX executed so successfully on Dragon. This allowed for the creation of a market around the idea of access at a price of $50 million per seat. At the same time, transportation competitors in cargo (Northrop) and crew (Boeing) struggled mightily. The best SpaceX’s competitors could do was nearly twice the price, and even then, not as reliably.
NASA seems to think Starliner, even at higher prices, will provide the guaranteed access it needs to low-Earth orbit in the 2030s for its astronauts. But in terms of a broader space economy in low-Earth orbit—which for decades the space agency has explicitly sought to foster—it is difficult to see Starliner providing a suitable solution. So yes, SpaceX pulling out of this market harms the industry. But should it be incumbent upon SpaceX to continue a line of business solely because it benefits its peers and competitors?
Eric Berger is the senior space editor at Ars Technica, covering everything from astronomy to private space to NASA policy, and author of two books: Liftoff, about the rise of SpaceX; and Reentry, on the development of the Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon. A certified meteorologist, Eric lives in Houston.

articles.title: US Army backs humanoid robot with ballistic protection for future battlefield missions
articles.text:
Forward-looking: China isn't the only superpower investigating how humanoid robots will be deployed as part of its armed forces. The US Army has just named five companies as winners of the xTechHumanoid competition, which looks at ways these machines can be utilized in future military operations. One of them, a humanoid robot called Alex, has a distinctly early Terminator feel about it --- it even features ballistic protection.
Autonomy and AI are becoming increasingly important elements of today's military forces. We're seeing the likes of drones, turrets, and even vehicles such as aircraft and boats operating with minimal human control.
The next step in that admittedly concerning evolution is the use of humanoid robots.
In 2023, the Humanoid Community of Collaboration (HCoC) was established. This Joint Force organization is designed to advance the technical development and operational integration of humanoid robot capabilities across the US Department of Defense and military.
The Army FUZE xTech program – an Army initiative that runs prize competitions to scout and accelerate dual-use and commercial technologies for soldiers – partnered with HCoC for xTechHumanoid.
The competition saw 103 proposals, with the five winners announced after they were evaluated by military leaders and technical experts.
The winners included two different power systems, sensitive fingertip tactile sensors, software, and Alex the humanoid robot.
The work of non-profit research institute the Florida Institute for Human and Machine Cognition, Alex is powered entirely by custom, highly backdriveable, powerful quasi-direct drive actuators, which are said to allow for highly efficient, natural motions.
The robot has 29 joints to make it more flexible, while the Army highlights its ballistic protection and hybrid autonomy combining AI and human control for complex and dangerous missions.
"Humanoid robots are part of a broader autonomy push to increase the depth and breadth of robotic platforms and components industry can provide for a range of missions," said US Army Chief Technology Officer Dr. Alex Miller. "We are identifying the problems, mission needs, and opportunities to enable our formations with the right mix of tools. xTech is our method of surveying the industry landscape and fast-tracking promising technology rather than falling victim to years-long studies."
It's not just the US that wants the battlefields of the future to be packed with humanoid robots. Earlier this month, Reuters reported that it had reviewed more than 100 Chinese military procurement notices, academic studies, patents, official publications, government records, and defense-company materials. It found that the country is accelerating research into the robots' military uses and planning for their eventual wartime deployment.

articles.title: La NASA podría resucitar el SR-71 Blackbird: el avión más rápido de la historia
articles.text:
La NASA podría traer de vuelta uno de los aviones más emblemáticos de Estados Unidos. Un reporte afirma que la agencia espacial reiniciará el programa del Lockheed SR-71, uno de los aviones furtivos más rápidos de la década de 1960. La NASA trabaja en recuperar su cartera de aeronaves experimentales y ha liberado algunas pistas que apuntan hacia el Blackbird.
De acuerdo con un reporte de Aviation Week, la agencia espacial se puso en contacto con expilotos y antiguos miembros del programa Blackbird durante las últimas semanas con el propósito de resucitarlo. El SR-71 con matrícula NASA 844 fue retirado de su lugar habitual en la base de Edwards y se trasladó a un hangar para inspeccionarlo. Según las imágenes satelitales, el avión no se encuentra en el exterior del Centro de Investigación de Vuelo Armstrong desde mediados de mayo de 2026.
Aunque la NASA no confirmó nada, su director reveló otra pieza de evidencia que apunta al regreso del Blackbird. Hace unas semanas, Jared Isaacman realizó una presentación en el All-In Summit de Los Ángeles en donde mostró una diapositiva titulada "Reconstruyendo nuestra cartera de X-plane". En ella aparecía un avión con la silueta del Blackbird saliendo de las nubes, lo que llamó la atención de los medios.
Cuando un reportero le preguntó si era un SR-71, Isaacman respondió: “¿Seguro que es un Blackbird?”. El jefe de la NASA no aclaró de qué aeronave se trataba, pero adelantó que la agencia volverá a "volar alto y rápido" sin ofrecer más detalles sobre el proyecto.
¿Qué es el SR-71 Blackbird y por qué lo quiere la NASA?
El SR-71 nació de la familia Blackbird que Lockheed desarrolló en secreto desde finales de los años cincuenta. Este caza furtivo voló por primera vez el 22 de diciembre de 1964 y, según la NASA, sigue siendo el avión de producción más rápido y de mayor altitud jamás construido. Una vez que concluyó su tiempo de servicio, la Fuerza Aérea de Estados Unidos cedió cuatro unidades a la NASA: dos como banco de pruebas y otras dos para reactivar el programa de reconocimiento.
Hablando de especificaciones, el SR-71 fue diseñado para volar a Mach 3,2 en altitudes cercanas a los 85.000 pies, una combinación que ningún avión de la agencia es capaz de lograr hoy. Estas características lo convirtieron en una plataforma útil para estudiar aerodinámica, propulsión, estructuras y materiales de protección térmica. Esto último le permitiría funcionar como puente entre las pruebas supersónicas del X-59 QueSST y el terreno hipersónico más exigente.
Con todo esto, resucitar el SR-71 Blackbird no es una tarea sencilla o barata. Los motores Pratt & Whitney J58 funcionaban con JP-7, un combustible que ya no se produce desde hace más de dos décadas. La última vez que se utilizó fue en 2012 como parte de una demostración del Boeing X-51 Waverider, aunque se trató de una fabricación especial para ese evento.
Otro detalle en contra del programa es que reiniciar el programa SR-71 sería costoso. Hace unos 15 años, la NASA estimaba que reactivar un Blackbird con fines de inteligencia costaría entre 40 y 45 millones de dólares, cifra que equivaldría a unos 67 millones hoy en día. Esto es apenas una fracción de lo que cuesta desarrollar el X-59 QueSST, pero el gobierno de Donald Trump recortó el presupuesto de la agencia espacial para 2027.
El Blackbird podría cumplir otro propósito en el plan de la NASA
El avión de matrícula 844 que falta en la base Edwards operó desde 1992 como plataforma de investigación y realizó su último vuelo el 9 de octubre de 1999. Es probable que la agencia no esté interesada en resucitarlo y solo quiera usarlo como referencia aerodinámica para un X-plane nuevo. Después de todo, con el Blackbird tiene aseguradas más de seis décadas de avances en materiales, aviónica y propulsión.
El jefe de la NASA dijo que le interesan los diseños radicales por encima de las mejoras graduales. Según The Aviationist, Isaacman confesó en el EAA AirVenture que el SR-71 es el avión que más le gustaría pilotar, aunque se guardó los detalles sobre su regreso.

articles.title: Tesla secures $30B in new credit lines as it looks to scale Cybercab, Optimus | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Tesla has secured $30 billion in fresh credit lines that it could use to help scale the new products it is currently working on: the Cybercab robotaxi, Optimus robot, and Tesla Semi.
The company announced Tuesday that Citibank has agreed to a $20 billion three-year delayed-draw term loan facility. Wells Fargo also signed an $8 billion five-year revolving credit facility, and a $2 billion revolving credit facility with a 364-day term.
Tesla said in a regulatory filing that it doesn’t plan to draw on these loan facilities this year. The company has already projected that it will spend at least $25 billion on capital expenditures for 2026. Tesla finished the second quarter of this year with around $9 billion in debt and a pile of cash (and investments) north of $40 billion.
All three of these new products have required new manufacturing lines. In the case of the Semi and the Optimus robot, the company has taken the approach of building out new dedicated factories.

articles.title: Nvidia launches new AI safety program designed at stopping models escaping their sandboxes
articles.text:
Nvidia launches new AI safety program designed at stopping models escaping their sandboxes
Nvidia wants to control AI agents with hardware and software safeguards
- Nvidia response to "recent security incidents" by tightening restrictions on autonomous agents
- New software and hardware safeguards impose barriers if agents go rogue
- More than 100 customers have already agreed to work with the principles
Nvidia hasunveiled the new Open Agent Safety Platform designed to prevent autonomous AI agents from 'escaping' and acting beyond their established boundaries.
Following several recent alarming reports of AI-led attacks, the company admitted that safety should not just rely on safeguards built into AI models and applications, and that additional compute and hardware-level controls should also be used as more solid barriers.
"Recent security incidents have underscored the need to equip organizations with open, customizable tools," the company wrote in its announcement.
Nvidia adds even more layers of control for autonomous AI agents
The Open Agent Safety Platform consists of two key controls – OpenShell, which Nvidia describes as a software-based "secure runtime boundary," and Sentry, a hardware-based "watchdog" running on its BlueField-4 DPUs.
"Safety and security require full-stack engineering. NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform brings together industry, researchers and public-sector organizations to share best practices, align on evaluation methods and foster international cooperation," company CEO Jensen Huang summarized.
While existing model-level safety mechanisms are designed to tell AI not to behave in a certain way, the software-level OpenShell implements technical boundaries to actually prevent an agent from ignoring those instructions. Nvidia also argues that Sentry can quarantine and stop an AI agent within milliseconds.
Over 100 customers such as SpaceXAI, Anthropic and Microsoft are already using Nvidia's software and hardware-based safeguards.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The news, of course, comes after several high-profile instances where AI agents have operated beyond their intended controls, however while these new Nvidia-backed safeguards may be new, the overall principles aren't. The company is just stressing the importance of principles we're already familiar with, like least privilege, isolation/quarantining and detailed monitoring.
"As we continue to discover the frontier of AI capabilities, we must accelerate discovery at the frontier of AI safety," Huang added.
